item.title: France Football chief hints at small margin between Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappé in Ballon d’Or race
item.description: France Football chief hints at small margin between Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappé in Ballon d’Or race France Football Editor-in-Chief Vincent Garcia, officially the only man in the world to know the identity of the Ballon d’Or winner before the ceremony, has revealed that Real Madrid and France international striker Kylian Mbappé went close to winning the 2025-2026 Men’s Ballon d’Or, which has been secured by Bayern Munich and England striker Harry Kane. Speaking to L’Equipe , Garcia said that Kane beat Mbappé to world football’s greatest individual prize by fewer than 41 points, which was the small gap that separated Vinicius Junior to Manchester City’s Rodri back in 2024. The Men’s Ballon d’Or is decided by 100 journalists – one from the top 100 nations in the FIFA rankings – who draw up their list of the ten best players from the past season. The player in first place receives 15 points, whilst the player in 10th place receives just one. Garcia also reveals that split votes to reward Spain’s World Cup triumph may have cost Lamine Yamal a better spot than third place, considering that Rodri was fourth in the 2025-2026 Men’s Ballon d’Or rankings. GFFN | Bastien Cheval

item.title: Johnny Manziel among former Texas football stars to stump with Trump
item.description: President Donald Trump will swing through Texas again on the campaign trail in the leadup to November's midterms. This time, he'll have some of the state's biggest former college football stars stumping with him. (AFP Contributor/AFP via Getty Images) With the November midterms drawing near, President Donald Trump appears to be pulling out all the stops to promote Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton 's bid for U.S. Senate. His newest allies on the campaign trail? Three former Texas college football standouts, according to a report published Monday by Axios. Axios' Alex Isenstadt reported Monday that former Texas A&M quarterback Johnny Manziel , former Texas Longhorns signal caller Colt McCoy and former New England Patriots star and Texas Tech alum Danny Amendola will join the president on the campaign trail on Tuesday in a multi-stop campaign blitz targeting Lubbock and Corpus Christi . The team-up may be surprising on its face, however, at least two of the former gridiron greats joining Trump this week have history with the president. In January of 2017 Manziel deactivated his Twitter (now X) account shortly after posting words of advice for the then-first-term president. "Yo @POTUS even I know to stay away from the notifications section on twitter. S--t will drive you crazy, lead the country and let them hate," Manziel wrote . Former Texas A&M star Johnny Manziel will be campaigning for Texas Republicans alongside President Trump this week, according to an Axios report. (Alex Slitz/Getty Images) Manziel later reactivated his X account, and in a 2024 interview with FOX News , remarked that he didn't see himself getting involved in politics. "Politics is probably something I will never get involved in," Manziel said in the wide-ranging interview. Amendola's connection to Trump can be publicly traced back to the Patriots' April 2017 visit to the White House. During the visit, which Amendola skipped in order to attend a friend's funeral, the president praised the wide receiver's play against the Atlanta Falcons in New England's come-from-behind Super Bowl LI victory. Amendola tweeted his thanks to the president, but later deleted the post in the face of digital backlash. Trump shouts out Danny Amendola, who wasn't at White House, and says, "Where's Danny?" Edelman doesn't help POTUS. https://t.co/skkQDXMlMx - Jeff Eisenband (@JeffEisenband) April 19, 2017 "Thanks for the shout out @realDonaldTrump! in the GYM! Funeral service for my boy Jaimie Carrillo tonight! RIP-JC," Amendola wrote. McCoy's connection to Trump is less straightforward. McCoy retired from the NFL in 2024 and began working in commercial real estate in Texas in 2025. Texas Governor Greg Abbott appointed the former Longhorns star to the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board (THECB) in January. item.title: Kirby Moore’s first season has been an abject failure
item.description: PULLMAN, WA - OCTOBER 24: Washington State Cougars head coach Kirby Moore walks on the outside of the huddle during a timeout in the game against the Boise State Broncos and the Washington State Cougars at Martin Stadium in Pullman, WA on October 24, 2026. (Photo by Oliver McKenna/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Hindsight being what it is, maybe it should’ve been easier to see this coming. On their third coach in three seasons with their depth pillaged like a Yukon gold rush stake left unprotected, expectations of the Washington State Cougars finishing at or near the top of the revamped Pac-12 were, perhaps, lofty. Not many programs could survive such turmoil without a substantial bump in the road, but given the retention and portal performance of the incoming coaching staff, reasons abounded to have some level of encouragement. The return of many of the best offensive playmakers? Check. A good defensive coordinator hire? Double check. Winning a portal battle for a quarterback sought after by at least one other Pac-12 institution? Triple check. A formula that, if nothing else, keeps the bottom from falling straight to the floor. Turns out, Kirby Moore is most comfortable on a deflated air mattress on top of linoleum. There’s really no other way about it: his first season at the helm of the Washington State Cougars has been an abject failure. A lone win over a startlingly small and slow Duquesne Dukes, the only notch in the pleather belt plucked from the waste bin of a knock off store, its the worst season on the Palouse in 17 years. An offense without an identity seemingly unable to effectively matriculate the ball for a lone first down, let alone into field goal range next to a defense that, while they play admirably to begin games, starts to quickly collapse under the sheer weight of the minutes required of them and the tightness of a unit that cannot make mistakes, lest their offense get the ball back with a need to score. An offensive coordinator demoted. A starting quarterback the same. An offense as putrid as any I’ve ever watched; no identity, no ability to execute, unable to block, shockingly lacking in athleticism. Third and shorts a mere dream, a magnificent wish as you watch this team play from behind the sticks again and again and again. “Abject failure” may actually be too generous of an evaluation. It is really and truly shocking how much has gone wrong for the Cougars this season. Set against the backdrop of the Oregon State Beavers running offensive roughshod over most of their opponents only adds to the gut-punch qualities of a year that, while perhaps an undefeated outlook was much too generous, eight wins was not. What makes this even more difficult is the failure is so widespread, so impossible to contain, pointing to any one thing as “There, that’s it!” is nigh on impossible. Kirby Moore is a first-time head coach and, to be sure, we should expect some first-time head coach growing pains.

(Photo by Oliver McKenna/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Hindsight being what it is, maybe it should’ve been easier to see this coming. On their third coach in three seasons with their depth pillaged like a Yukon gold rush stake left unprotected, expectations of the Washington State Cougars finishing at or near the top of the revamped Pac-12 were, perhaps, lofty. Not many programs could survive such turmoil without a substantial bump in the road, but given the retention and portal performance of the incoming coaching staff, reasons abounded to have some level of encouragement. The return of many of the best offensive playmakers? Check. A good defensive coordinator hire? Double check. Winning a portal battle for a quarterback sought after by at least one other Pac-12 institution? Triple check. A formula that, if nothing else, keeps the bottom from falling straight to the floor. Turns out, Kirby Moore is most comfortable on a deflated air mattress on top of linoleum. There’s really no other way about it: his first season at the helm of the Washington State Cougars has been an abject failure. A lone win over a startlingly small and slow Duquesne Dukes, the only notch in the pleather belt plucked from the waste bin of a knock off store, its the worst season on the Palouse in 17 years. An offense without an identity seemingly unable to effectively matriculate the ball for a lone first down, let alone into field goal range next to a defense that, while they play admirably to begin games, starts to quickly collapse under the sheer weight of the minutes required of them and the tightness of a unit that cannot make mistakes, lest their offense get the ball back with a need to score. An offensive coordinator demoted. A starting quarterback the same. An offense as putrid as any I’ve ever watched; no identity, no ability to execute, unable to block, shockingly lacking in athleticism. Third and shorts a mere dream, a magnificent wish as you watch this team play from behind the sticks again and again and again. “Abject failure” may actually be too generous of an evaluation. It is really and truly shocking how much has gone wrong for the Cougars this season. Set against the backdrop of the Oregon State Beavers running offensive roughshod over most of their opponents only adds to the gut-punch qualities of a year that, while perhaps an undefeated outlook was much too generous, eight wins was not. What makes this even more difficult is the failure is so widespread, so impossible to contain, pointing to any one thing as “There, that’s it!” is nigh on impossible. Kirby Moore is a first-time head coach and, to be sure, we should expect some first-time head coach growing pains. Bad clock management? No coach in the world is immune. Late subs and uneven performances? You bet. Punting from midfield in a season already lost? That’s the full give up flag, baby. A season that is merely slightly disappointing would not bring out the microscopes, but Kirby Moore has invited us to throw open the cupboards of the lab rooms in Fulmer Hall and empty them onto the counter. He’ll get another season at the helm of this football team; you can be sure of that. Washington State isn’t in the habit of firing coaches after one season, and trying to find your fourth in four years is inadvisable, to say the least. But what we’ve seen so far isn’t impressive. It’s not even hopeful. It’s downright appalling. The overhaul of the offensive coaching staff in the offseason has to be total. Who Kirby Moore chooses to bring in behind them is for him to figure out, but my gentle suggestion of “no one who is your friend” would be a good one to heed. It’s clear no coach can be back on that side of the football. Once you’ve done that, spending most available resources on offensive linemen and wide receivers is an absolute must. These shouldn’t be suggestions, mind you. It’s Jon Haarlow’s job to make sure his coach understands what’s at stake as they head into their second season together. Lest you think their fates are not tied together, they almost certainly are. Generally speaking, athletic directors don’t get an opportunity to hire another football coach after they have to fire their first. It’s tough to say that, no matter what happens for the remainder of the season, it doesn’t really matter. Wazzu is into what should’ve been the easiest part of their schedule, but another win or two, no matter how unlikely, changes nothing. This is still the worst Washington State football season in nearly two decades. And Kirby Moore better spend the offseason ensuring it isn’t a repeat.

item.title: The Old Lady Speaks Podcast, Episode 361: Juventus get a long-awaited win in Serie A
item.description: LECCE, ITALY - OCTOBER 25: Weston McKennie of Juventus FC after scoring a goal to make it 0-1 during the Serie A match between US Lecce and Juventus at Stadio Via del Mare on October 25, 2026 in Lecce, Italy. (Photo by Ivan Romano/Getty Images) | Getty Images Juventus hadn’t won a Serie A fixture in well over a month. And as much as a lengthy international break played into it, it’s not like the way Juve had been playing of late warranted anything other than dropped points following their Sept. 20 victory over Atalanta prior to the break. That month-plus without a win in Serie A is, thankfully, now a thing of the past. Juventus won for their first time in Serie A in nearly a month and a half with Sunday night’s 2-0 victory over Lecce. It was not exactly exciting. It was not exactly a crisp kind of performance — especially in the second half as Juve tried to hold off the clear momentum that Lecce had in front of their home crowd at the Via del Mare. Juventus bent. Oh, they most certainly bent. But they didn’t break. Thankfully they did — and got the three points that comes with it. You can listen to Episode 361 of The Old Lady Speaks Podcast on the player below or your favorite podcast platform. No matter how you listen, we appreciate your continued support. To our dear listeners: Please look for the latest episode of The Old Lady Speaks Podcast to drop every Monday morning/afternoon for those of you who live in the United States. (Please adjust your time zone accordingly if you live outside of the U.S. or Canada.) If you happen to listen to the Old Lady Speaks Podcast on Apple Podcasts or Spotify , please subscribe to the show and give us a nice five-star rating and maybe even a sweet review because it is very nice to see that our podcast is being enjoyed by you all. The more you say nice things about us, the more we will continue to love you forever and ever and ever. We promise.

item.title: Brewers' Pat Murphy Shares Heartwarming Reason For Bringing Kids To Postgame Press Conferences
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy Since the Milwaukee Brewers made Pat Murphy the manager, they have been playing on another level. He has won back-to-back National League Manager of the Year Awards and is basically a lock to win his third in a few weeks. Murphy has proven he is an elite manager after a long journey to simply get the opportunity in the big leagues. He is two wins away from the World Series, but he has maintained the same goofy, honest and straightforward personality he has had for his whole career. Murphy has become known for keeping things light while also maintaining a high standard of play. He preaches toughness, but also cares deeply about his players and organization, no matter how hard of a time he gives them. However, at his core, he is a family man, and that can be seen in his press conferences. Murphy has consistently brought his kids to his postgame press conferences, and while it may not seem like a big deal, Murphy explained the deeper meaning behind doing so. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! "I just want them to know that I'm the same no matter what," Murphy told reporters on Monday . "If we're in A-ball next year... I'm there for them the same every single day, and they're the priority. It's wonderful to have family around." Sometimes it's easy to forget that players and managers are regular people like everyone else. Like most, Murphy cares deeply for his family, and a small thing like bringing his kids to the podium with him actually carries a significant purpose. More MLB: Brewers Doing Something For First Time All Year In Game 3 Of World Series

item.title: What ‘really upset’ former Red Sox manager Alex Cora about getting fired
item.description: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images What ‘really upset’ former Red Sox manager Alex Cora about getting fired appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Former Boston Red Sox manager Alex Cora opened up publicly Monday about his April firing, explaining how the decision affected people beyond himself. His comments came six months after chief baseball officer Craig Breslow dismissed him during a disappointing start to the season. Boston also removed several coaches , making the change broader than a managerial replacement. Baseball Is Dead’s Tyler Milliken shared a clip Monday on X, formerly Twitter, from Cora’s extended interview on the popular Baseball Isn’t Boring podcast with its co-founder, Rob Bradford. The former Red Sox manager explained what upset him most about his firing. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “The thing that really upset me that Saturday was that other guys paid the price. Not only the coaches, but I felt like you know the players paid the price because you gotta you take away a whole group from from an equation, and it’s gonna take time.” Alex Cora opened up about his firing and explained that what really upset him was other people paid the price. Both coaches and players. For a small sample size. Cora tipped his cap to Breslow for having conviction. Noted Breslow’s “doubts” about the program. 🎥: @BBisntBoring pic.twitter.com/iLkXBkadf9 — Tyler Milliken (@tylermilliken_) October 26, 2026 The Red Sox dismissed Cora on April 25 with a 10-17 record that left the team last in the American League East. Breslow, owner John Henry and president Sam Kennedy traveled to Baltimore to deliver the decision. Cora said a text from Breslow at the team hotel alerted him to the meeting. The Red Sox also fired hitting coach Peter Fatse, third base coach Kyle Hudson, bench coach Ramon Vazquez, assistant hitting coach Dillon Lawson and hitting strategy coach Joe Cronin. Boston also reassigned Jason Varitek, who has not been with the organization since. Milliken’s post also noted that Cora credited Breslow’s conviction while acknowledging the executive’s doubts about the program. Their tension dated back at least to the 2025 season. The Red Sox subsequently clinched their second consecutive playoff berth under Chad Tracy, who became permanent manager on September 22. Cora remains under contract through 2027 and is unlikely to manage next season, though he has not ruled it out. His comments shed light on the staff shakeup as Boston moves forward under Tracy.

item.title: NFL rumors: 49ers, Bears targeting defensive line help at trade deadline, including some surprises
item.description: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images NFL rumors: 49ers, Bears targeting defensive line help at trade deadline, including some surprises appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . NFL observers seem to suggest the San Francisco 49ers need to pursue Maxx Crosby. And the Bears have been mentioned as a team that could use Khalil Mack . Both teams are targeting defensive line help at the trade deadline, including some surprises , according to a post on X by Jordan Schultz. “I think we’re headed toward a very active trade deadline,” Schultz said. “We could see anywhere from 12 to 20 trades. And two teams I’m watching very closely: the 49ers and Bears. I’ve heard both teams connected to several defensive players. Including rushers Josh Sweat, Khalil Mack. Also, DeForest Buckner. Some names who aren’t necessarily on the trade block. I think both Chicago and San Francisco, they want to be aggressive. And I’d be shocked if they don’t make a move before the deadline.” Will the 49ers make a splash trade? Among the names mentioned as possible targets for the 49ers is Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr. He showed a ton of potential as a rookie, but has fallen out of favor with the Jaguars. There are plusses and minuses with this player, according to 49erswebzone.com. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “For San Francisco, Thomas would offer another potential big-play threat and a long-term piece at a position where the team will eventually have to make some difficult decisions,” Marc Adams wrote. “Of course, the 49ers would need to determine whether his current struggles are a product of Jacksonville’s offense, his own development, or some combination of the two.” However, Buckner seems like the better fit . He’s frustrated with the Colts, according to NBC Sports. “I’m sick and tired of the same song and dance every year,” Buckner said. “We lost to the Tennessee Titans, who were 0-5, and now they’re 1-5. “Every single person on the team needs to be critics of themselves and figure out what we need to do better,” Buckner said. There seems to be a fire inside of Buckner, and that would make him a plus for the 49ers. They’re seeking a Super Bowl run while the Colts (2-5) seem to be spinning their wheels — again — as Buckner said. item.content:encoded: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images NFL rumors: 49ers, Bears targeting defensive line help at trade deadline, including some surprises appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . NFL observers seem to suggest the San Francisco 49ers need to pursue Maxx Crosby. And the Bears have been mentioned as a team that could use Khalil Mack . Both teams are targeting defensive line help at the trade deadline, including some surprises , according to a post on X by Jordan Schultz. “I think we’re headed toward a very active trade deadline,” Schultz said. “We could see anywhere from 12 to 20 trades. And two teams I’m watching very closely: the 49ers and Bears. I’ve heard both teams connected to several defensive players. Including rushers Josh Sweat, Khalil Mack. Also, DeForest Buckner. Some names who aren’t necessarily on the trade block. I think both Chicago and San Francisco, they want to be aggressive. And I’d be shocked if they don’t make a move before the deadline.” Will the 49ers make a splash trade? Among the names mentioned as possible targets for the 49ers is Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr. He showed a ton of potential as a rookie, but has fallen out of favor with the Jaguars. There are plusses and minuses with this player, according to 49erswebzone.com. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “For San Francisco, Thomas would offer another potential big-play threat and a long-term piece at a position where the team will eventually have to make some difficult decisions,” Marc Adams wrote. “Of course, the 49ers would need to determine whether his current struggles are a product of Jacksonville’s offense, his own development, or some combination of the two.” However, Buckner seems like the better fit . He’s frustrated with the Colts, according to NBC Sports. “I’m sick and tired of the same song and dance every year,” Buckner said. “We lost to the Tennessee Titans, who were 0-5, and now they’re 1-5. “Every single person on the team needs to be critics of themselves and figure out what we need to do better,” Buckner said. There seems to be a fire inside of Buckner, and that would make him a plus for the 49ers. They’re seeking a Super Bowl run while the Colts (2-5) seem to be spinning their wheels — again — as Buckner said. item.title: Dallas Cowboys come to agreement for DCC after unionizing
item.description: Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Dallas Cowboys come to agreement for DCC after unionizing appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Dallas Cowboys had a “meaningful discussion” and came to an agreement with the newly formed Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders union. According to The Dallas Morning News, the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Association (DCCA) has been recognized by the Cowboys as “the collective bargaining representative for the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders,” according to the press release. The union follows years of the DCC speaking out about disparity in pay despite being one of the top dance squads worldwide. The DCC has been a focal point in the Netflix series America’s Sweethearts for the last three seasons, where the cheerleaders have brought up the topic on several occasions. In season one, DCC star Kat Puryear compared her DCC yearly salary to a full-time Chick-fil-A worker or a substitute teacher. In season two, the discussions continued, which later resulted in the team announcing that they would be receiving a 400% raise in the season two finale. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) In 2010, the Cowboys were the defendants in a fair-wage lawsuit filed by Erica Wilkins, who was a three-year veteran on the squad. She claimed that she made $16,000 in her highest-earning year with the team. America’s Sweethearts will be back on the streamer for season four as announced back in August. “Each new season is another opportunity to showcase the extraordinary talent, dedication and individuality of our team,” Kelli Finglass said in a release at the time. “We’re proud to continue to share their stories and artistry with audiences, inspiring the next generation of young performers all over the world to dream big and pursue their passions.” It’s unclear if or how the union will be addressed on the new season. At this time there has been no word on the details of the agreement nor when season four will premiere. In the meantime, the first three seasons of America’s Sweethearts are available to stream on Netflix now. Related: Kylian Mbappé, Jorja Smith all smiles during Ballon d’Or encounter Related: Pat McAfee reveals every reason he hated Utah ‘College GameDay’ visit

item.description: The Seattle Seahawks have rediscovered their primetime magic in home games over the past couple of seasons, and what a way to snap a losing skid! They throttled the Kansas City Chiefs in a barely competitive 20-3 win, putting themselves back in the NFC West chase and sending a message to the NFL that, as long as they don’t sabotage themselves with turnovers, they’re extraordinarily hard to beat. Hell, they’re hard to beat even when they do commit a bunch of turnovers! This was a doubly sweet weekend for Seahawks fans, with the San Francisco 49ers suffering an upset loss to the Atlanta Falcons. You know what that means! Enemy Reaction is back for the first time since Week 2—we skipped over the Los Angeles Chargers—and there is a healthy bonus meltdown coming from 49ers fans. Chiefs game thread comments are courtesy of Arrowhead Pride ! This was a doubly sweet weekend for Seahawks fans, with the San Francisco 49ers suffering an upset loss to the Atlanta Falcons. You know what that means! (20-3 SEA FINAL) That was niiiiice 😮‍💨 TOUCHDOWN EMANUEL WILSON. 📺: @SNFonNBC pic.twitter.com/YfJgdXKJ4Y — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 26, 2026 Post-game: The Chiefs 5-0 start looks suspect ( Vahe Gregorian, KC Star ) Early on, anyway, the 2026 Chiefs sure were trending toward redemption and resumption of their modern identity as a perennial championship contender. In the wake of the distressing 6-11 dud last season, they entered Sunday night’s game against reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle at Lumen Field as one of just two remaining undefeated NFL teams. Moreover, they led the league in offensive yards per game, were second in points allowed and generally seemed to be restoring the new world order of the Mahomes Era. But their 20-3 loss to the Seahawks (4-3) was so thorough, unsightly and disillusioning as to render the 5-0 run-up to it entirely suspect — especially considering the Chiefs’ thorny schedule ahead. Yes, Seattle is a fine team and the ol’ one-game overreaction is a real phenomenon when it comes to NFL games. No doubt the Chiefs are capable of resetting. Trouble is, this loss seemed to expose every worrisome vulnerability they had flashed in beating teams with a combined record of 11-22. And it also came with the deflating issue of the stifling of something we were starting to take for granted: the exhilarating play of former Seahawks running back Kenneth Walker III, who had been a revelation until he mustered just 36 yards on 14 carries Sunday. An inconsistent offensive line couldn’t make room for Walker. Post-game video: The biggest need for the Chiefs going forward (96.5 The Fan) Is WR, DL or OT the biggest need for the #Chiefs going forward? pic.twitter.com/uczCRxsSZ7 — 96.5 The Fan (@TheFan965) October 26, 2026 BONUS Enemy Reaction: San Francisco 49ers Cookin' with the SAUCE 🔥 @DrakeLondon_ FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/ljV4yxVwac — Atlanta Falcons (@AtlantaFalcons) October 25, 2026 BOOM! @KendalDaniels__ picks it off! FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/7VBExpgNMh — Atlanta Falcons (@AtlantaFalcons) October 25, 2026 GEORGE KITTLE LOSES THE BALL AND THE FALCONS WILL WIN THE GAME! pic.twitter.com/JOpGjkEbbI — TSN (@TSN_Sports) October 25, 2026 Enemy Preaction: Chicago Bears RHAMONDRE STEVENSON‼️ 📺 Prime Video pic.twitter.com/heXDiTFnzW — New England Patriots (@Patriots) October 23, 2026 SANTOS JUST DRILLED A 58-YARDER TO GO UP TWO POSSESSIONS. NEvsCHI on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/XgUaLFdlzS — NFL (@NFL) October 23, 2026 Alright, so the Seahawks aren’t condemned to an early offseason just yet. They’ve gone through a rough patch and still come out the other side of it with a winning record. Up next are the Chicago Bears, who are 5-2 with a more potent offense (on paper) than the Chiefs. Mike Macdonald vs. Ben Johnson. ‘The Dark Side’ versus Caleb Williams, D’Andre Swift, Luther Burden, Colston Loveland, and local legend Rome Odunze. Dennis Allen’s defense against a Seahawks offense that showed signs of life. What a way to wrap up three straight nationally televised games, and what a way to kick off November with one more primetime showdown at Lumen Field! If the Seahawks prevail, then they’ll have withstood the toughest part of their schedule and still reached 5-3. All things considered, that would be pretty encouraging. Thanks for reading and go ‘Hawks!

item.title: Cason Wallace to have surgery, could miss rest of the 2026-27 NBA season
item.description: Cason Wallace started the 2026-27 NBA season by getting a lucrative contract extension to stay in Oklahoma City with the Thunder as they looked to make another run to the NBA Finals. Sadly, those hopes just took a major blow less than a full week into the season. Thunder GM Sam Presti announced on Monday that Wallace has suffered a torn labrum and will require surgery. With a long recovery timetable, a return this season looks bleak for the former Kentucky Wildcats standout. Wallace has become a core player for the Thunder alongside SGA in the backcourt. Already winning one title, it seems this team’s window is still wide open with how many draft picks they have accrued over the next several seasons. However, it will take a lot for them to make another deep run this season, especially with teammate Jalen Williams also being sidelined for most, if not the entire season due to a dislocated ankle and fractured fibula. Here’s to hoping both of these guys are able to fully heal and return at some point this season. BREAKING: Oklahoma City's Jalen Williams has a dislocated left ankle and fractured fibula; Cason Wallace has a torn labrum in his left shoulder. Both will undergo surgery and be sidelined for several months — most, if not the entire season. pic.twitter.com/62OxZtIGRc — Shams Charania (@ShamsCharania) October 26, 2026

item.title: Michael Carrick fights on as Man United manager after surviving initial crisis talks
item.description: Michael Carrick remains left in the dark but will stay on as Manchester United manager for now after surviving talks between the club’s hierarchy on Monday. Carrick had appeared to be on the brink of the sack following the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth on Sunday and technical director Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada met to discuss his future at the club’s Carrington training ground and sound out potential replacements. Carrick then arrived at the training ground shortly before 2pm on Monday afternoon, just in time to watch the club’s Under-21s play a behind-closed-doors match against Hull, before he left Carrington a few hours later. (Getty) But the popular former midfielder – who was backed by the United supporters at Old Trafford despite the abject defeat to Bournemouth – remains in charge and is continuing to prepare for this weekend’s trip to Chelsea in the Premier League as usual. United’s first-team squad will be back at Carrington for training on Tuesday, which is expected to be led by Carrick. That’s despite United’s hierarchy reportedly sounding out potential replacements for Carrick if they are required to appoint a fourth permanent manager in the three years since the minority Ineos ownership took control of football operations from the Glazers. Former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann , the ex-Bayern Munich and Germany head coach, are both available and are considered the frontrunners for the job if Carrick is sacked. Aston Villa’s Unai Emery and Brighton’s Fabian Hurzeler are admired but their clubs would demand significant compensation. The United supporters made clear who they blame for the club’s worst start to a league season in 40 years and longest winless run since 2015 as they turned on the players and chanted against the Glazers, co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Ineos hierarchy, including director of football Wilcox, on Sunday. Carrick made the decision to drop Bruno Fernandes and leave him on the bench following the captain’s criticism of his manager’s tactics, a move that appeared to receive support from the United fans as they did not chant for the Portuguese to be introduced despite the humbling to Bournemouth. Former United defender Gary Neville accused the United players of “downing tools”, meanwhile, as the progress they made under Carrick last season has spectacularly unravelled and revealed a fractured dressing room. (Getty) “Michael Carrick is a brilliant man,” Neville said on Sky Sports . “He's a man of integrity, of credibility, of decency, of professionalism, of high-quality football and consistency and reliability. Everything the group of players in that dressing room aren’t. “I know that because if Bruno has turned on him publicly, with that little statement, imagine what they're like behind the scenes. item.content:encoded: Michael Carrick remains left in the dark but will stay on as Manchester United manager for now after surviving talks between the club’s hierarchy on Monday. Carrick had appeared to be on the brink of the sack following the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth on Sunday and technical director Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada met to discuss his future at the club’s Carrington training ground and sound out potential replacements. Carrick then arrived at the training ground shortly before 2pm on Monday afternoon, just in time to watch the club’s Under-21s play a behind-closed-doors match against Hull, before he left Carrington a few hours later. (Getty) But the popular former midfielder – who was backed by the United supporters at Old Trafford despite the abject defeat to Bournemouth – remains in charge and is continuing to prepare for this weekend’s trip to Chelsea in the Premier League as usual. United’s first-team squad will be back at Carrington for training on Tuesday, which is expected to be led by Carrick. That’s despite United’s hierarchy reportedly sounding out potential replacements for Carrick if they are required to appoint a fourth permanent manager in the three years since the minority Ineos ownership took control of football operations from the Glazers. Former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann , the ex-Bayern Munich and Germany head coach, are both available and are considered the frontrunners for the job if Carrick is sacked. Aston Villa’s Unai Emery and Brighton’s Fabian Hurzeler are admired but their clubs would demand significant compensation. The United supporters made clear who they blame for the club’s worst start to a league season in 40 years and longest winless run since 2015 as they turned on the players and chanted against the Glazers, co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Ineos hierarchy, including director of football Wilcox, on Sunday. Carrick made the decision to drop Bruno Fernandes and leave him on the bench following the captain’s criticism of his manager’s tactics, a move that appeared to receive support from the United fans as they did not chant for the Portuguese to be introduced despite the humbling to Bournemouth. Former United defender Gary Neville accused the United players of “downing tools”, meanwhile, as the progress they made under Carrick last season has spectacularly unravelled and revealed a fractured dressing room. (Getty) “Michael Carrick is a brilliant man,” Neville said on Sky Sports . “He's a man of integrity, of credibility, of decency, of professionalism, of high-quality football and consistency and reliability. Everything the group of players in that dressing room aren’t. “I know that because if Bruno has turned on him publicly, with that little statement, imagine what they're like behind the scenes. If that's your captain saying that, imagine what they're saying in the dressing room behind closed doors when no one's listening. That's horrific. "There's a few of them that don't go to bed at the right time, don't eat the right things, don't think about Manchester United every single minute of every day, and aren't living and breathing this football club as they should be - and as professionals should. “Why? Because it's gone to their heads. But they still walk around like King William. They are nothing, some of those players.” (Getty) Carrick initially returned to Old Trafford as interim manager – his second stint in caretaker role – after the dismissal of Ruben Amorim at the beginning of the year. He was rewarded with the full-time position after guiding United to third in the Premier League last term and securing a return to the Champions League. United spent £155m on three new midfielders this summer – signing Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andre Santos, after missing out on their top targets Elliott Anderson and Sandro Tonali – but failed to sign a back-up left-back to Luke Shaw or another forward to support the injury-prone Benjamin Sesko. Lisandro Martinez criticised the club’s hierarchy for not doing more to support Carrick following the 2-1 defeat to Atletico Madrid earlier this month while Fernandes questioned his manager’s tactics following the 4-1 loss at Como last week. Carrick said Fernandes did not play against Bournemouth due to “pure football” reasons while the Portuguese was also present at Carrington on Monday, reportedly for pre-planned treatment on a pre-existing injury. United will travel to Chelsea on Saturday before playing back-to-back home games before the international break, welcoming Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday and Aston Villa the following Sunday in the Premier League. There are then two weeks before United face a trip to Anfield to play Liverpool on Sunday 22 November.

item.title: Former Trevecca basketball player Jon Burch named new Trojans AD
item.description: Former McGavock and Trevecca basketball player Jon Burch will replace longtime Trojans athletic director Mark Elliott on July 1, 2027. Elliott, who has led the school's athletic department for 16 years, announced his retirement in late July, effective at the end of the 2026-27 academic year. Burch will become Trevecca's 14th athletic director. Trevecca president Dan Boone made the announcement Oct. 26. Burch will work alongside Elliott to further develop his vision for the department until Elliott retires. Burch has a long history at Trevecca. After graduating from McGavock, he played basketball for Trojans Hall of Fame coach Frank Wilson. Burch served in the Navy, then returned to Trevecca to complete his education, including a doctorate in education in 2003. He has taught management and leadership at Trevecca for 26 years at the undergraduate, master’s and doctoral levels in the Skinner School of Business. Burch also serves as Trevecca's NCAA faculty athletics representative. He presently works with Elliott, the athletics leadership staff and the coaches to support student-athletes. “Jon has loved Trevecca athletics from the time he was a student to where he is today, as the faculty athletics representative and a parent of one of our students,” Boone said in a statement. “His selection resolves any concern about finding someone who’s a good fit for Trevecca.” MARK ELLIOTT RETIRING FROM TREVECCA: Trevecca athletic director Mark Elliott will retire in 2027 “Trevecca athletics has a strong foundation," Burch said. "Mark Elliott has intentionally anchored the department in the Christian-scholar-athlete philosophy. That philosophy excites me, and I fully embrace it. I appreciate Dr. Boone’s trust in me with this new opportunity. The quality of our coaches, staff, and leadership team already points to great days ahead for our student-athletes and everyone in the TNU and Nashville communities who loves Trojan athletics.” “I am incredibly grateful that Jon has agreed to serve as our next athletics director,” Elliott said. “As a dedicated, long-term member of our university community, a professor of management and leadership, and our faculty athletics representative, he already commands deep respect from our coaching staff.” Reach Mike Organ at 615-259-8021 or on X @MikeOrganWriter. This article originally appeared on Nashville Tennessean: Former Trevecca basketball player Jon Burch named new Trojans AD

item.title: Kane beats Yamal and Mbappe to taste Ballon d'Or glory
item.description: Spain's Luis de La Fuente won the men's coach of the year (FRANCK FIFE) Harry Kane became England's first Ballon d'Or winner in 25 years in his native city of London on Monday, beating out stiff competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe. Alexia Putellas claimed the women's prize for a third time to extend Spain's domination of the award, thanks to her role in leading Barcelona to last season's Champions League before moving to London City Lionesses. The first ever Ballon d'Or ceremony on English soil got off to an inauspicious start as the London traffic caused a delay of nearly an hour, with many of the star names arriving late. But there was a happy ending for the hometown hero as Kane collected the crowning glory of his career to date, becoming the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001. The 33-year-old Bayern Munich forward struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, propelling the German giants to a league and cup double. He also scored six times as England finished third at the World Cup. "I love to represent my country and to bring this trophy back to them and have an English winner I think is something that's really, really special, especially here in London," Kane told AFP. "What a crazy night and I'm really, really happy." Despite being England and Tottenham's all-time record goalscorer, Kane's medal collection is limited to German domestic triumphs. He was on the losing side for Spurs in the 2019 Champions League final against Liverpool and twice tasted bitter defeat in the final of the European Championship with England. But joining Bayern in 2023 and his remarkable goalscoring consistency have earned him the highest individual award in football. "Making the move to Bayern Munich was a big step in my career," Kane told AFP earlier. "Some people saw it as a risk but for me it was always about improving and seeing if I could get better around the team-mates, the team, the club and it has pushed me onto another level. "Being a number nine for Bayern and England you are expected to score goals and to do that the number of times I did last year is something I'm really proud of," he added. - Putellas back on top - The winner in 2021 and 2022, Putellas's third Ballon d'Or caps her return to the top of the women's game after an anterior cruciate ligament injury derailed her rise four years ago. Putellas succeeds Spain team-mate Aitana Bonmati, the winner the past three years whose season was quashed by a leg break. "This is a consequence of all that we achieved last season," said Putellas. item.content:encoded: Spain's Luis de La Fuente won the men's coach of the year (FRANCK FIFE) Harry Kane became England's first Ballon d'Or winner in 25 years in his native city of London on Monday, beating out stiff competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe. Alexia Putellas claimed the women's prize for a third time to extend Spain's domination of the award, thanks to her role in leading Barcelona to last season's Champions League before moving to London City Lionesses. The first ever Ballon d'Or ceremony on English soil got off to an inauspicious start as the London traffic caused a delay of nearly an hour, with many of the star names arriving late. But there was a happy ending for the hometown hero as Kane collected the crowning glory of his career to date, becoming the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001. The 33-year-old Bayern Munich forward struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, propelling the German giants to a league and cup double. He also scored six times as England finished third at the World Cup. "I love to represent my country and to bring this trophy back to them and have an English winner I think is something that's really, really special, especially here in London," Kane told AFP. "What a crazy night and I'm really, really happy." Despite being England and Tottenham's all-time record goalscorer, Kane's medal collection is limited to German domestic triumphs. He was on the losing side for Spurs in the 2019 Champions League final against Liverpool and twice tasted bitter defeat in the final of the European Championship with England. But joining Bayern in 2023 and his remarkable goalscoring consistency have earned him the highest individual award in football. "Making the move to Bayern Munich was a big step in my career," Kane told AFP earlier. "Some people saw it as a risk but for me it was always about improving and seeing if I could get better around the team-mates, the team, the club and it has pushed me onto another level. "Being a number nine for Bayern and England you are expected to score goals and to do that the number of times I did last year is something I'm really proud of," he added. - Putellas back on top - The winner in 2021 and 2022, Putellas's third Ballon d'Or caps her return to the top of the women's game after an anterior cruciate ligament injury derailed her rise four years ago. Putellas succeeds Spain team-mate Aitana Bonmati, the winner the past three years whose season was quashed by a leg break. "This is a consequence of all that we achieved last season," said Putellas. "I am really grateful for having been (at Barcelona) 14 seasons as a player, it is something incredible. It was like a perfect story." Yamal made the boldest fashion statement of the contenders with a pink flower on the front of his black suit. The Barcelona winger scooped up the first award of the night for young talent of the year for the third consecutive time. But the 19-year-old fell short of becoming the youngest ever Ballon d'Or winner, finishing third, after he failed to produce his best form during Spain's World Cup success. Mbappe finished second but his wait to win the Ballon d'Or goes on despite being the top scorer in the World Cup, Champions League and La Liga as his goals did not lead to collective triumphs for France or Real Madrid. Luis de la Fuente beat out Paris Saint-Germain's Luis Enrique and Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta to be named men's coach of the year after leading Spain to World Cup glory. "This is recognition for a job very well done over many years," De la Fuente told AFP. "I believe Spanish football, both in terms of coaching and the game itself, serves as an example of excellent youth development, which ultimately paves the way for future success." Barcelona's Pere Romeu scooped the prize for women's coach of the year. Paris Saint-Germain missed out on any of the main individual awards despite winning a second consecutive Champions League, but did have the consolation of men's club of the year. Spanish duo Unai Simon and Cata Coll were named best men's and women's goalkeeper. kca/gj

item.title: What’s got McAfee so fired up about the University of Utah?
item.description: Salt Lake City, UT - October 24, 2026 - President's Circle: on the set of College GameDay Built by the Home Depot at the University of Utah. | Rich Storry / ESPN Images Pat McAfee has made a career out of being loud, unpredictable and willing to get under people’s skin. But after spending Saturday morning at the University of Utah for ESPN’s “College GameDay,” the former NFL punter-turned-ESPN-superstar says he left with a feeling he rarely experiences on the road: discomfort. McAfee unloaded on the university during Monday’s episode of “The Pat McAfee Show,” saying a social media post mocking him and an awkward interaction during his million-dollar kicking contest combined to make for an experience he would rather not repeat. “I did not enjoy the University of Utah,” McAfee said Monday. The comments came two days after the “GameDay” broadcast from the Salt Lake Valley ahead of Utah’s matchup with Houston . The show brought its usual mix of college football analysis, fan interaction and celebrity appearances with former Utes star turned Buffalo Bills standout Dalton Kincaid as the guest picker, but the morning also produced several moments that apparently left McAfee with a bad taste. The biggest issue, he said, started before the cameras even went live. The post that set him off According to McAfee, he was getting ready to appear on “GameDay” when he saw a video on the university’s Instagram account featuring students doing impressions of him . One student called him “corny.” Another described him as “creepy.” McAfee said he would have had no problem with students making fun of him on their personal social media accounts. What bothered him was that the video appeared on an official university account shortly before he was scheduled to promote the school to a national audience. “If these kids would have done this on their own vlogs, all good,” McAfee said. “I mean, everybody’s taking shots at me anyways for everything. I get it.” His issue was the source of the criticism, not necessarily the criticism itself. “The university puts that out?” he said. “Like, as I’m about to go out and do an infomercial for the place?” McAfee said the timing made him question how the university viewed his presence on campus. He was preparing to walk in front of thousands of Utes fans while representing the school on one of college football’s biggest broadcasts, only to see the university’s social media account poke fun at him. “It’s the university putting this out,” he said. “It’s not like a vlog. item.content:encoded: Salt Lake City, UT - October 24, 2026 - President's Circle: on the set of College GameDay Built by the Home Depot at the University of Utah. | Rich Storry / ESPN Images Pat McAfee has made a career out of being loud, unpredictable and willing to get under people’s skin. But after spending Saturday morning at the University of Utah for ESPN’s “College GameDay,” the former NFL punter-turned-ESPN-superstar says he left with a feeling he rarely experiences on the road: discomfort. McAfee unloaded on the university during Monday’s episode of “The Pat McAfee Show,” saying a social media post mocking him and an awkward interaction during his million-dollar kicking contest combined to make for an experience he would rather not repeat. “I did not enjoy the University of Utah,” McAfee said Monday. The comments came two days after the “GameDay” broadcast from the Salt Lake Valley ahead of Utah’s matchup with Houston . The show brought its usual mix of college football analysis, fan interaction and celebrity appearances with former Utes star turned Buffalo Bills standout Dalton Kincaid as the guest picker, but the morning also produced several moments that apparently left McAfee with a bad taste. The biggest issue, he said, started before the cameras even went live. The post that set him off According to McAfee, he was getting ready to appear on “GameDay” when he saw a video on the university’s Instagram account featuring students doing impressions of him . One student called him “corny.” Another described him as “creepy.” McAfee said he would have had no problem with students making fun of him on their personal social media accounts. What bothered him was that the video appeared on an official university account shortly before he was scheduled to promote the school to a national audience. “If these kids would have done this on their own vlogs, all good,” McAfee said. “I mean, everybody’s taking shots at me anyways for everything. I get it.” His issue was the source of the criticism, not necessarily the criticism itself. “The university puts that out?” he said. “Like, as I’m about to go out and do an infomercial for the place?” McAfee said the timing made him question how the university viewed his presence on campus. He was preparing to walk in front of thousands of Utes fans while representing the school on one of college football’s biggest broadcasts, only to see the university’s social media account poke fun at him. “It’s the university putting this out,” he said. “It’s not like a vlog. It’s the actual place that we’re at.” The university’s social media post has since been deleted. It remains unclear who approved the video or whether the post was intended to be anything more than a lighthearted attempt to engage with students. McAfee, however, said it affected how he felt heading into the broadcast. “I’ve never been more uncomfortable, honestly, in my life walking in front of a group of people after watching their university put out a post basically dogging me just moments before,” he said. Sports Business Journal’s Austin Karp said it was unusual for a university account to post something like that. “It seems very unusual for a school’s official account to take a shot at a broadcast partner like that, especially when a show like GameDay brings so much national publicity to the school, campus, athletic department and city,” Karp said. He noted, however, that the video came from a student group, which may not have been considering the broader relationship between ESPN and the Big 12. The million-dollar kick didn’t help The social media video was only part of the morning’s awkwardness. McAfee also pointed to an exchange during his popular “Kicking is Easy” segment, which gives a selected fan the opportunity to make a field goal for a $1 million prize. The contest took on a different life the previous weekend when “GameDay” visited the BYU Cougars for their matchup with Notre Dame. BYU student Carter Smith, dressed as Spider-Man, missed his first kick, but got another shot and nailed it . He walked away with $3 million after Utah Jazz and Mammoth owner Ryan Smith and his business partner, Ryan Sweeney, matched the original $1 million prize. ONE MORE KICK CARTER #CollegeGameDay https://t.co/bTxno8VIZ8 pic.twitter.com/bt24KNOQog — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) October 17, 2026 Utah student Morgan Boring, a chemical engineering major and swimmer who said she had never kicked a football before, was selected for the contest the following week. Before attempting the kick, Boring brought up the previous week’s payout. “Wait, wait, wait, the BYU guy got $3 million,” she said. The exchange was awkward, and McAfee appeared annoyed during the interaction , saying that he could have offered her only $20 instead. Boring ultimately missed her $1 million dollar kick. On Monday, McAfee referenced the moment as another reason the morning did not sit well with him. “And then obviously the kicker goes, ‘Only $1 million?’” he said. “It’s my money. ‘Only $1 million?’ It’s like, all right, I hate this place.” The contrast between the two visits was hard to ignore. Over at BYU, the show had delivered a memorable moment with a student snagging life-changing money and the whole campus going wild. But a week later, the awkward question about the cash turned into just another headache for McAfee. A bigger reason for discomfort There was another, more serious reason McAfee said the university’s social media post made him uncomfortable. During Monday’s show, he referenced the killing of Charlie Kirk at Utah Valley University in Orem in September 2025. “Has anything like really scary happened at like a college gathering in the state of Utah recently?” McAfee asked rhetorically. He later returned to the point, saying the university’s actions felt particularly uncomfortable given what had happened in Utah a little more than a year earlier. That was key for him. McAfee wasn’t just upset about kids poking fun at him. He felt like the university’s post, combined with the timing and everything else going on, made walking out in front of the crowd feel super awkward. “Just didn’t like the university taking a shot at me,” he said. He also noted that he is accustomed to criticism and that he understands why some people dislike him, acknowledging that he has plenty of qualities people might find irritating. But he drew a line between criticism from individuals and what he viewed as criticism coming from an institution he was there to promote. The university hasn’t responded to McAfee’s comments as of Monday. A different experience from BYU McAfee’s reaction also stands out because it followed a successful visit to BYU just one week earlier. “GameDay” returned to Provo for the first time since 2009, setting up on campus ahead of the Cougars’ top-10 matchup with Notre Dame. The episode averaged 3 million viewers , making it the third-most-watched broadcast in the show’s history, per ESPN. Utah followed with its own nationally televised showcase ahead of a ranked matchup with Houston. The university had a chance to put its campus, football program and fans in front of a national audience, and the student section made a strong impression on McAfee. He didn’t suggest the entire experience was a failure. In fact, he was quick to praise the football program and the atmosphere. “They do have an incredible student section from my understanding, and they have a good football team,” he said. He also described Saturday’s broadcast as phenomenal. But his comments made clear that he viewed the two Utah visits very differently, even if the programs and their fans were not entirely responsible for every moment that unfolded. Will McAfee return to Utah? For now, McAfee is making it clear that he has little interest in repeating the experience. “I’ll hopefully never go to that place,” he said Monday, later joking that he might have COVID-19 the next time “College GameD

item.title: Roberto Clemente's widow saw Francisco Lindor's award coming
item.description: ST. PERTERSBURG, FL — Luis Clemente remembers what his mother said after she met Francisco Lindor. "I remember when Mom told me that this young man is going to be someone very, very important in representing our country," he said, "and she was right." On Monday, Luis Clemente was on hand as Lindor was given the award named for his father. The New York Mets shortstop received the 2026 Roberto Clemente Award presented by Capital One at Tropicana Field before Game 3 of the World Series between the Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers. Lindor is the fifth winner of Puerto Rican descent, joining Edgar Martinez (2004), Carlos Delgado (2006), Carlos Beltrán (2013) and Yadier Molina (2018), players he said he studied and tried to follow. "I'm glad there was people in life like Clemente, like Carlos Delgado … that set the path for me," Lindor said. "I just follow them." Capital One is giving $100,000 in his honor to SEEN Foundation, a youth organization with which Lindor and his wife, Katia, work. Commissioner Rob Manfred first noticed in April 2018. MLB sent the Minnesota Twins and Cleveland to San Juan for two games, seven months after Hurricane Maria, and filled the trip with community events. Lindor ran a clinic for about 250 kids at his old elementary school in Gurabo. The next night he homered in front of a sellout crowd at Hiram Bithorn Stadium. "My friend here, I think, attended every single one of those events," Manfred said, "and it really left an impression on me." Why Francisco Lindor won the Roberto Clemente Award Lindor was 12 when he left Puerto Rico for Montverde Academy, a boarding school just west of Orlando, with limited English. He has given the school more than $1 million since 2020, most of it for Lindor Hall, a two-story middle school building with science and technology labs. A scholarship in his name covers tuition for kids who couldn't otherwise attend. This year he started Lindor's Leaders with New Balance, mentoring students in Bayside High School's sports medicine program on leadership, communication and mental health. Some of those students thanked him on video during Monday's ceremony. So did families he had hosted in his suite at Citi Field. Every fall he hands out hundreds of backpacks in Queens. Lindor Smile Tuesdays, in its third season, brings youth groups to Citi Field to learn about dental health. After Hurricanes Maria and Fiona, he paid for relief in Puerto Rico and restored athletic facilities in his hometown of Caguas. "For me, I love education, and she loves the health side of things," Lindor said of Katia, whom he called "the rock." "We don't really try to be recognized by the work we do in the communities," he said. "But there is something that we get out of it." What is the Roberto Clemente Award? MLB began honoring players for community work in 1971 with the Commissioner's Award. item.content:encoded: ST. PERTERSBURG, FL — Luis Clemente remembers what his mother said after she met Francisco Lindor. "I remember when Mom told me that this young man is going to be someone very, very important in representing our country," he said, "and she was right." On Monday, Luis Clemente was on hand as Lindor was given the award named for his father. The New York Mets shortstop received the 2026 Roberto Clemente Award presented by Capital One at Tropicana Field before Game 3 of the World Series between the Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers. Lindor is the fifth winner of Puerto Rican descent, joining Edgar Martinez (2004), Carlos Delgado (2006), Carlos Beltrán (2013) and Yadier Molina (2018), players he said he studied and tried to follow. "I'm glad there was people in life like Clemente, like Carlos Delgado … that set the path for me," Lindor said. "I just follow them." Capital One is giving $100,000 in his honor to SEEN Foundation, a youth organization with which Lindor and his wife, Katia, work. Commissioner Rob Manfred first noticed in April 2018. MLB sent the Minnesota Twins and Cleveland to San Juan for two games, seven months after Hurricane Maria, and filled the trip with community events. Why Francisco Lindor won the Roberto Clemente Award Lindor was 12 when he left Puerto Rico for Montverde Academy, a boarding school just west of Orlando, with limited English. He has given the school more than $1 million since 2020, most of it for Lindor Hall, a two-story middle school building with science and technology labs. A scholarship in his name covers tuition for kids who couldn't otherwise attend. This year he started Lindor's Leaders with New Balance, mentoring students in Bayside High School's sports medicine program on leadership, communication and mental health. Some of those students thanked him on video during Monday's ceremony. So did families he had hosted in his suite at Citi Field. Every fall he hands out hundreds of backpacks in Queens. Lindor Smile Tuesdays, in its third season, brings youth groups to Citi Field to learn about dental health. After Hurricanes Maria and Fiona, he paid for relief in Puerto Rico and restored athletic facilities in his hometown of Caguas. "For me, I love education, and she loves the health side of things," Lindor said of Katia, whom he called "the rock." "We don't really try to be recognized by the work we do in the communities," he said. "But there is something that we get out of it." What is the Roberto Clemente Award? MLB began honoring players for community work in 1971 with the Commissioner's Award. It was renamed in 1973 for Clemente, the Hall of Famer and 15-time All-Star who died in a plane crash on New Year's Eve 1972 while delivering supplies to earthquake victims in Nicaragua. Every team nominates one player. Lindor has been the Mets' nominee four years running. A panel that included Manfred and Clemente's three sons, Enrique, Luis and Roberto Jr., chose him from this year's 30. "We call it the highest award because it recognizes a unique combination," Manfred said. "Excellence on the field and community service." Lindor, a five-time All-Star with four Silver Sluggers and two Gold Gloves, talked mostly about other people. "This award represents me, but also it represents my family," he said. "It represents my mom." Luis Clemente said the best way to honor his father is to treat kids "like they are someone now, not who they become later." "Ultimately that's what life is all about," Lindor said. "Taking care of the people that actually need guidance and help." item.title: Thomas Tuchel sends message to Harry Kane after winning Ballon d’Or
item.description: Thomas Tuchel says he has “run out of superlatives” to describe Harry Kane after the England captain won the Ballon d’Or . Bayern Munich striker Kane pipped Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe to football’s most prestigious individual prize at the London Palladium, rewarded for his staggering season in which he scored 73 goals for club and country. The 33-year-old became the first Englishman to lift the trophy since Michael Owen in 2001. Harry Kane won the Ballon d’Or on Monday night (AFP/Getty) Under Tuchel, he led his country to the last four of the World Cup, where they suffered a devastating loss to Argentina. England nevertheless achieved their best World Cup finish since 1966, coming home with bronze after victory over France in the third-place play-off. Following Kane’s triumph, Tuchel said: “Congratulations Harry on a deserved Ballon D’Or! “I ran out of superlatives to describe your performances a long time ago, but I’m delighted to see that you have now been formally recognised by the football world. “To become the first Englishman to win this huge honour in 25 years makes it extra special and we are lucky to have you as our leader. “I know you will enjoy this moment with your loved ones and then get back to doing what you do best – scoring goals and winning football matches.” The FA also honoured Kane’s Ballon d’Or win by illuminating the Wembley arch in gold on Monday night. Wembley Stadium’s arch was illuminated in gold to honour Kane’s triumph (Getty) Kane paid tribute to his England team-mates, manager and staff during an emotional acceptance speech . “To all my England teammates, we had a special year,” he said. “It wasn't the perfect year, but we had a lot of good moments. We built a great bond together, a lot of togetherness. The way we trained, the way we played, the togetherness in the hotel in the World Cup. “It’s truly an honour to captain you, lead you. It makes me extremely proud so this one is for all of us, for sure. “To Thomas Tuchel and the staff at England again. The leadership, the way you drive us, the way you push standards is something to be admired and it's an honour to represent you and represent the England badge the way you do. “I know Debbie [Hewitt, FA Chair] is here tonight as well, so Debbie, thank you very much for everything you do and everyone at the FA, it's truly an honour to be your captain.”

The leadership, the way you drive us, the way you push standards is something to be admired and it's an honour to represent you and represent the England badge the way you do. “I know Debbie [Hewitt, FA Chair] is here tonight as well, so Debbie, thank you very much for everything you do and everyone at the FA, it's truly an honour to be your captain.”

item.title: 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan ‘optimistic’ Christian McCaffrey’s hamstring will be okay after the bye
item.description: Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan ‘optimistic’ Christian McCaffrey’s hamstring will be okay after the bye appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Coach Kyle Shanahan ’s San Francisco 49ers are getting a bye week at the perfect time amid a sea of injuries that cost them their perfect record in a Week 7 loss to the Atlanta Falcons, which included a Christian McCaffrey injury scare. Blame was assigned for the 49ers’ loss, including to QB Brock Purdy who had a costly interception that was snagged by Jessie Bates of Atlanta. Following the loss, Cam Inman of the Bay Area News Group shared notes from coach Shanahan on McCaffrey and others, and it sounded like good news for the all-world running back. “McCaffrey has a mild hamstring strain, not thigh. Optimistic he’ll be OK for Raiders game post-bye,” Inman wrote. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Also expected back (but not guaranteed) after bye are WRs (Mike) Evans, (Deebo) Samuel, DE (Nick) Bosa, LB (Luke) Gifford; S (Marques Sigle), DT (CJ) West.” Shanahan added that no kicker tryouts are in the works. The 49ers are 6-1 on the season despite tough-luck injuries, and have been encouraged to shake things up with a potential trade for Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby . Purdy is still the NFL’s quarterback rating GOAT , but he is only human and made mistakes amid a hailstorm of injuries against Atlanta. The 49ers need a healthy McCaffrey to play to their full potential. He has become more durable over the last few seasons, but the NFL is a rough league and no one knows what the future holds. Shanahan did his best to quell injury concerns, now it’s time for San Francisco to heal up. Week 9 will bring a home game against the Raiders that looks like another opportunity to move toward home field advantage throughout the playoffs for one of the NFL’s best and most star-studded teams. Related: NFL rumors: 49ers, Bears targeting defensive line help at trade deadline, including some surprises Related: 49ers most to blame for shocking upset loss to Falcons

item.title: How worried should Spurs be amid sluggish 1-2 start?
item.description: How worried should Spurs be amid sluggish 1-2 start? originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Perhaps overshadowed by the Knicks ' 0-3 start, the Spurs have looked vulnerable in their first three games after winning the Western Conference last season. San Antonio got back in the win column against the Cooper Flagg-less Mavericks on Saturday, but the Spurs started 0-2 with losses to the Thunder and Rockets with Victor Wembanyama put together one of the worst offensive performances of his career against Oklahoma City. After beating all expectations last season, the Spurs are now facing a championship-or-bust campaign and might be showing that matching those steep expectations isn't easy. Here's a look at what the start of the season says about the Spurs. How worried should Spurs be? Despite a 1-2 start, the Spurs shouldn't sound the alarm. This is a team still figuring out how to operate with Dylan Harper in the starting lineup with De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle, and it's understandable if that dynamic takes some time to fully come together. Both Harper and Fox have played fairly well to start the season. Wembanyama's inefficiency has been a much bigger problem. While it might be fair to wonder whether Wembanyama is capable of making the leap to MVP, there is no doubt he is going to round back into form at some point soon; he isn't someone the Spurs have to worry about. The Spurs will also have free-agent addition Tobias Harris back from injury in the near future, which should give Mitch Johnson another player who grabs offensive rebounds and helps the younger guys. Another reason to avoid panicking about the Spurs is the situation around them. The West doesn't seem to be as deep as the East, meaning San Antonio isn't at as much risk of sliding down the standings with a stumble here and there, and the long-term injuries to Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace are a serious blow to a Thunder team that entered the season as the Spurs' top competition in the West. A team in the East could theoretically be swallowed up after a tough start. With as much talent as the Spurs have, the West just isn't deep enough for a rocky start to derail the season. STREAM : Watch Spurs games with DAZN What's gone wrong for the Spurs? The Spurs haven't gotten the best play out of Wembanyama, who is shooting just 36.5 percent from the field. Sometimes it's that simple: your best players have to play their best, and Wembanyama hasn't. San Antonio is also shooting less than 32 percent from 3-point range, which is bound to change at some point. That ranks above some of the NBA's worst marks through the first week of the season, but it's more than 10 percentage points behind the unbeaten Timberwolves and Lakers . Expect that to balance out a bit in the near future. item.title: Panthers lose veteran tackle Taylor Moton indefinitely to leg injury
item.description: The Carolina Panthers must turn the page quickly after a 30-point loss to the Tampa Bay Bucs Sunday. The Panthers’ next game is on Thursday, and they’ll be without one of their leaders. Veteran offensive tackle Taylor Moton is now out indefinitely. Sunday was his second game back after a lengthy recovery from blood clots. Moton suffered a separate injury Sunday when he fractured a bone in his lower leg. He’s one of the Panthers’ longest-tenured players and a trusted voice in the locker room. Head Coach Dave Conales spoke about the injury. “Myself, his teammates, we’re all hurt for T-Mo, but we know what he represents and how he battled to get back out there and in the process, was just there for his teammates,” the coach said. READ MORE: Bucky Irving runs for 2 TDs and Bucs force 4 turnovers in 43-13 rout of Panthers You can watch the Panthers’ matchup against the Green Bay Packers Thursday night on Channel 9. We’ll have a special edition of Panthers Gameday live from Green Bay. Our pregame coverage starts at 7 p.m. right here on Channel 9. Then stay with us after the game for our postgame show, followed by WSOC Tonight.

item.title: Harry Kane ends England’s 25-year wait for Ballon d’Or winner
item.description: Harry Kane has won the Ballon d’Or and best striker awards - Action Images/Matthew Childs “Wow, wow, wow,” Harry Kane said as he took to the stage at the London Palladium after winning the 2026 Ballon d’Or. Wow indeed. “I am speechless,” Kane added before launching into a heartfelt speech, the wobble in his voice showing just how much this meant to him. In truth it would have been a travesty if the 33-year-old England captain – and Bayern Munich striker – had not won with his family, friends and coaches all watching from the stalls at this iconic old theatre. “All those years of sacrifice,” he said of his parents, Pat and Kim, his voice faltering more than ever at that moment. It was from the heart. And faltering again as he spoke about his wife and “best friend” Katie Goodland. “This is a trophy we all celebrate,” he said, talking to his children back in Bavaria. “I bring a few others [trophies] home but this one is a special one.” Kane described his wife Katie Goodland as his “best friend” - Shutterstock/Tolga Akmen Kane ’s speech was as outstanding as his football. “Lastly for me it is the journey,” he said. “Learn through resilience, determination and self-belief. My journey was not easy and I had to fight my way to be the very best right now. I hope that can give you inspiration.” So much for the “one-season wonder”. So much for the doubters who poured scorn on him. So much for those who believed he would never make it after loan spells at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich City and Leicester City. With varying degrees of success. Kate Scott, the presenter, perfectly detected the emotion and said: “You held it together. You got through it.” It showed how much it meant to Kane, who simply and quietly replied, “Yes”. October 26, 2026 What a winner. What a player. What a role model. The award given in the city where he has scored most of his goals. But he would not have been in the running for this accolade had he not been brave enough to quit Tottenham Hotspur after 19 years and move to Germany. Kane was the favourite. But, despite its prestige, the Ballon d’Or process is an odd one. One journalist from each of the top-100-ranked Fifa countries is given a vote, with the organisers, France Football, laying out the criteria: individual performance, collective performance and fair play. In that order. They often go for the biggest name. Not the best. Kane’s numbers are incredible. They speak for themselves. His numbers show he deserved to win the prize: 65 games for club and country and 73 goals. Plus eight assists (for the judging period – August 3, 2025 to July 19, 2026). That is 61 goals for Bayern and 12 for England. That is a goal less than every 72 minutes. That is beyond elite. That is world-class and legendary. Bayern Munich and England's Ballon d'Or winner doing what he does best 🎯 https://t.co/yWNburqkpg — Match of the Day (@BBCMOTD) October 26, 2026 For his club, that is 19 goals more than any other player in the top five European league
