You got through it.” It showed how much it meant to Kane, who simply and quietly replied, “Yes”. October 26, 2026 What a winner. What a player. What a role model. The award given in the city where he has scored most of his goals. But he would not have been in the running for this accolade had he not been brave enough to quit Tottenham Hotspur after 19 years and move to Germany. Kane was the favourite. But, despite its prestige, the Ballon d’Or process is an odd one. One journalist from each of the top-100-ranked Fifa countries is given a vote, with the organisers, France Football, laying out the criteria: individual performance, collective performance and fair play. In that order. They often go for the biggest name. Not the best. Kane’s numbers are incredible. They speak for themselves. His numbers show he deserved to win the prize: 65 games for club and country and 73 goals. Plus eight assists (for the judging period – August 3, 2025 to July 19, 2026). That is 61 goals for Bayern and 12 for England. That is a goal less than every 72 minutes. That is beyond elite. That is world-class and legendary. Bayern Munich and England's Ballon d'Or winner doing what he does best 🎯 https://t.co/yWNburqkpg — Match of the Day (@BBCMOTD) October 26, 2026 For his club, that is 19 goals more than any other player in the top five European leagues. And the most since Cristiano Ronaldo scored 61 for Real Madrid in 2014-15. Kane won last season’s Golden Shoe by nine goals from Erling Haaland. He reached his century of Bundesliga goals last month in just 98 games, destroying Dieter Müller’s record set 49 years ago. He took 129 matches. Kane became one of only two players in history (the other is Ronaldo) to score 20-plus goals across World Cups and European Championships and was the only one to score in two major club cup finals, including a hat-trick. Neither Kylian Mbappé nor Lamine Yamal, his closest rivals, scored in any finals. Both gave interviews declaring why they should win the Ballon d’Or. Kane? “I don’t like talking about myself,” he said. “The 73 goals speak for themselves.” They do. Those are the facts, but there is also the football and, yes, the conduct. Kane has scored some simply superb goals during that period, not least for England. Take his brace against the Democratic Republic of Congo at the World Cup to rescue his team and Thomas Tuchel. Kane scored six times at the World Cup to help England finish third - Getty Images/Julian Finney Kane, the first English player since Michael Owen in 2001 to win the award, is also the ultimate team player – so fulfilling that “collective performance” criteria – and a captain who leads by example. On and off the pitch. Fair play? He was last booked in January and was cautioned just three times in 68 games and not at all in any of his 13 appearances this season. And he works hard. So very hard. Kane was in the top 10 for total distance covered at the World Cup, despite playing a game fewer than most of the others on the list. And he is often seen winning as many defensive headers in his own penalty area as attacking ones in the opposition’s. That work extends to off the pitch, to try to maximise his ability, to do everything to be the best version of himself and to be the best. Which he has now been recognised as. And it stems from his winning mentality. Some scoffed when Kane walked into England’s press conference before the 2018 World Cup and said he could be top-scorer. And then did just that. October 26, 2026 They probably also scoffed at the notion that he would one day be declared the best player in the world and win the Ballon d’Or. But he has done all that. It confirms England’s all-time cap holder (for now jointly with Peter Shilton) and goalscorer as one of the greats. And we are privileged to witness that greatness. The Bayern Munich striker, in his home city, becomes the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001. “First of all, I am almost speechless. Lucky I have this list. It being in London is extra special and felt like a good omen. Thanks to those who voted for me, as it would have been tough this year. Congratulations to all the nominees and winners tonight. “Thanks to my teammates who are here tonight. It is an honour to play for Bayern Munich and represent you. I want to say thank you to Tottenham Hotspur as well. I would not be where I am today without Tottenham. You allowed me to live my dream. “I want to give a shout-out to some of my coaches down the years. You all played important roles at different stages of my career. item.title: Kane prematurely announced as Ballon d'Or winner - but he wasn't only one
item.description: Harry Kane has become the first Englishman since 2001 to win the Ballon d'Or [Getty Images] Harry Kane was crowned winner of the men's Ballon d'Or on Monday night, but a few hours earlier that confirmation appeared to have been announced prematurely. At 17:15 GMT, an article from the award's official website titled 'Harry Kane wins the 2026 Ballon d'Or' began to circulate online. The widespread sharing of the article caused confusion online, with some wondering whether France Football - the organisers of the award - had fallen short at the final hurdle of keeping the winner, who was voted for by journalists at the end of September, under wraps. That was until further digging on the Ballon d'Or website revealed that some of the other favourites to win the award - including Barcelona's Lamine Yamal, Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe - also had similar pieces penned and published about them. When asked about the articles by BBC Sport, a Ballon d'Or spokesperson said: "Some profiles of nominees prepared by BallonDor.com were inadvertently published online. "These articles had been prepared for all nominees and should in no way be considered as an indication of the final results or rankings." By 17:40, the articles about Kane and Mbappe had been removed from the website. Similar articles were also written about London City Lionesses star Alexia Putellas and Barcelona's Ewa Pajor. Putellas went on to be officially confirmed as the winner of the women's Ballon d'Or. That premature announcement may have sparked some excitement in Kane that this could be his year, but he only had to wait a little longer to find out for sure. Kane ends England's 25-year Ballon d'Or wait - how he bucked the trend Putellas wins record-equalling third Ballon d'Or Listen to the latest Football Daily podcast

item.title: Kane ends England's 25-year Ballon d'Or wait - how he bucked the trend
item.description: Harry Kane broke Bayern Munich's goalscoring record for a season in his third campaign at the club [Getty Images] Harry Kane has become the first English player to win the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen in 2001 after being crowned the world's best player at a ceremony in London. The 33-year-old Bayern Munich striker is the fifth Englishman to win in total, with Stanley Matthews (1956), Bobby Charlton (1966) and Kevin Keegan (1978 and 1979) the others. Denis Law of Scotland (1964) and Northern Ireland's George Best (1968) are the other winners from the United Kingdom. Real Madrid and France forward Kylian Mbappe finished second, while Barcelona and Spain attacker Lamine Yamal completed the top three. "Not many people would have thought it, and maybe even I wouldn't have thought I'd be this far," Kane told Dazn. "I had to go through many ups and downs, especially early in my career. I was never the person that people thought was going to be the superstar like some of the guys now. "I had to bide my time and work hard, a lot of times it was me against my own mind and I had to come through it, I had to show self-belief, determination. "I think that grounded me even when I did make it at the highest level to keep improving and keep getting better." England manager Thomas Tuchel said he was "delighted" to see Kane win the award as he hailed the forward's success as a "huge honour". Prince William, meanwhile, said the former Tottenham Hotspur player was a "brilliant captain" and "remarkable player". Kane scored 61 goals in 51 club matches last season, the most a Bayern player has ever struck in one campaign. Including England matches, it was 73 goals - plus eight assists - in 65 matches. Only one player at a club in Europe's top five leagues has ever scored more goals in a season. But he wins it despite not lifting either of football's biggest prizes last season, having lost in both the World Cup and Champions League semi-finals. Remarkably the Three Lions captain becomes the first Bayern player to win the Ballon d'Or since Karl-Heinz Rummenigge in 1981. To celebrate Kane's success, the Wembley arches were lit up in gold on Monday night. BBC Sport looks at why Kane won it and how unusual it is to do so without securing one of those major trophies. England's greatest international? Kane is now a serious contender Putellas wins record-equalling third Ballon d'Or Kane's record-breaking 2025-26 season In terms of trophies, Kane may have 'only' lifted the German double last season. But that more than doubled his career trophy total - having also won the Bundesliga the season before. But in terms of individual output Kane - whose previous best Ballon d'Or finish was 10th - was unmatched last season. His 61 goals in all competitions for Bayern was 19 more than any other player in Europe's top five leagues managed. In fact it was the most anyone has recorded since Cristiano Ronaldo also notched 61 for Real Madrid 11 years ago. He was the Bundesliga's top scorer

Denis Law of Scotland (1964) and Northern Ireland's George Best (1968) are the other winners from the United Kingdom. Real Madrid and France forward Kylian Mbappe finished second, while Barcelona and Spain attacker Lamine Yamal completed the top three. "Not many people would have thought it, and maybe even I wouldn't have thought I'd be this far," Kane told Dazn. "I had to go through many ups and downs, especially early in my career. I was never the person that people thought was going to be the superstar like some of the guys now. "I had to bide my time and work hard, a lot of times it was me against my own mind and I had to come through it, I had to show self-belief, determination. "I think that grounded me even when I did make it at the highest level to keep improving and keep getting better." England manager Thomas Tuchel said he was "delighted" to see Kane win the award as he hailed the forward's success as a "huge honour". Prince William, meanwhile, said the former Tottenham Hotspur player was a "brilliant captain" and "remarkable player". Kane scored 61 goals in 51 club matches last season, the most a Bayern player has ever struck in one campaign. Including England matches, it was 73 goals - plus eight assists - in 65 matches. Only one player at a club in Europe's top five leagues has ever scored more goals in a season. But he wins it despite not lifting either of football's biggest prizes last season, having lost in both the World Cup and Champions League semi-finals. Remarkably the Three Lions captain becomes the first Bayern player to win the Ballon d'Or since Karl-Heinz Rummenigge in 1981. To celebrate Kane's success, the Wembley arches were lit up in gold on Monday night. BBC Sport looks at why Kane won it and how unusual it is to do so without securing one of those major trophies. England's greatest international? Kane is now a serious contender Putellas wins record-equalling third Ballon d'Or Kane's record-breaking 2025-26 season In terms of trophies, Kane may have 'only' lifted the German double last season. But that more than doubled his career trophy total - having also won the Bundesliga the season before. But in terms of individual output Kane - whose previous best Ballon d'Or finish was 10th - was unmatched last season. His 61 goals in all competitions for Bayern was 19 more than any other player in Europe's top five leagues managed. In fact it was the most anyone has recorded since Cristiano Ronaldo also notched 61 for Real Madrid 11 years ago. He was the Bundesliga's top scorer with 36 goals - 17 clear of anyone else. In the Champions League he scored 14 for the beaten semi-finalists. In the German Cup he scored 10 goals, including a hat-trick in the 3-0 win over Stuttgart in the final, and he also netted once in the German Super Cup. No player has ever scored so many goals in a season for Bayern, a club who have had legendary goalscorers like Gerd Muller, Rummenigge and more recently Robert Lewandowski in their ranks. Kane's 12 goals for England last season - including six at the World Cup - take him up to a total of 73. Only one player in history from Europe's top leagues has scored more in a season, Lionel Messi's 82 for Barcelona and Argentina in 2011-12. Next on the list are Muller (72 in 1972-73), Cristiano Ronaldo (66 in both 2011-12 and 2014-15), former Brazil striker Ronaldo (66 in 1996-97), Erling Haaland (64 in 2022-23) and Luis Suarez (64 in 2015-16). Former England striker Alan Shearer recently told BBC Sport: "The winner of the Ballon d'Or should be Harry Kane. "His numbers for the last 12 to 18 months have been absolutely sensational for Bayern and for England. For that reason, he should get it." Another ex-Three Lions player Danny Murphy added: "His goalscoring has been relentless, brilliant. He's had one of the best seasons of his career and it'll be a great reward for him if he gets the trophy. "He's been brilliant at Bayern Munich since he's been there, adapted really well and he's been the best centre forward in the world for the last 12 months." How rare is winning Ballon d'Or without a top trophy? The Ballon d'Or was only available to European players from its formation in 1956 until 1995 when it was opened up to everyone. Since then in four of the seven World Cup years, the Ballon d'Or has been awarded to a world champion - including Messi in 2023 (as the 2022 World Cup was in the winter). However, that was the first time since 2006 it had happened, with Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo and Luka Modric all winning since then despite not winning the World Cup that year. This is only the fifth time in the past 20 years that the Ballon d'Or has not gone to a player who has won either the World Cup, the Champions League or a European Championship/Copa America - with Kane joining Messi (three times) and Ronaldo. Lamine Yamal, who won the World Cup with Spain, had been one of the favourites but lost out to Kane. Last year, winning the Champions League helped PSG and France's Ousmane Dembele to the crown. Could Kane make it two in a row? Kane may have just won the Ballon d'Or but some are already wondering if he is in a good place to retain it next year. The striker has scored 10 goals in his opening 12 games for Bayern this season. Throw in six goals in four Nations League games for England and that is a total of 16 in 16 matches so far. Bayern are unbeaten in the Bundesliga and Champions League this season. If they were to win a Treble - and Kane keeps scoring at about a goal a game - it would be tough to look past him, especially in a season with no World Cup, European Championship or Copa America. The last player other than Messi or Ronaldo to win it two years in a row was Marco van Basten in 1988 and 1989. However, Lamine Yamal will be hoping to make it third time lucky after finishing second twice in two years. He has started the season in electric form, with 10 goals and 10 assists in 13 games for Barcelona in La Liga and the Champions League. And Barca are currently favourites to win the Champions League, which could ultimately end up being a deciding factor. He would be the youngest player to win the Ballon d'Or - aged 20 - if he does lift it next year. Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe will also fancy his chances of winning for the first time, with 14 goals in 13 appearances for club and country. The youngest winner remains Brazilian Ronaldo, who was 21 when he won in 1997. Arsenal, who have never had a Ballon d'Or winner, and Paris St-Germain are two of the other frontrunners to win the Champions League. 73 goals from dropping deep - we ask Kane to break down how he did it Kane prematurely announced as Ballon d'Or winner - but he wasn't only one

item.title: In Bermuda, a sudden-death playoff ended with no loser
item.description: Austin Smotherman won the playoff in Bermuda but Seamus Power got what he came for. Getty Images Austin Smotherman waited 100 PGA Tour events to get his first win . He needed just 57 holes to grab his second, beating Seamus Power on the third hole of a sudden-death playoff on Monday at the weather-shortened Butterfield Bermuda Championship. The win adds another year onto Smotherman’s full-time PGA Tour exempt status. His win at the Bank of Utah Championship gave him job security and a spot in the PGA Tour’s Championship Series when it begins in 2028. This win extends that through 2029. The victory in windy Bermuda also moved him up to No. 51 in the FedEx Cup Fall standings , putting him in position to earn starts at the first two Signature Events of 2027. Even Bermuda’s 40-mph gusts couldn’t extinguish the fall’s hottest player. “We knew we were doing a lot of good stuff and just wanted to go play golf,” Smotherman said of his attitude entering the FedEx Cup Fall after failing to make the FedEx Cup Playoffs. “We were excited for the fall season. We had our best FedEx Cup finish ever and the fall we felt was just going to be bonus golf and do things like this, and to have it come true and live this out now not once but twice in that short time frame is, I mean, I couldn’t have drawn it up. It’s a fairy tale, really.” Smotherman’s triumph in Utah was a victory 10 years in the making. He worked his way up from PGA Tour America (then called PGA Tour Latinoamerica) to the Korn Ferry Tour and then finally earned full-time PGA Tour status for the 2021-2022 PGA Tour season. Smotherman played three consecutive seasons on the PGA Tour before losing his card after finishing 169th in the FedEx Cup standings in 2024. But he bounced back, winning twice on the Korn Ferry Tour in 2025 to earn his card again. Smotherman played solid golf in his return to the PGA Tour in 2026, and he almost won the Cognizant Classic in March before finally kicking down the door in start No. 100 in Utah. Two weeks later, another win arrived, and with it proof of what Smotherman had long believed — something that can be invaluable as he looks to keep climbing the PGA Tour ladder. “It can literally happen at any time,” Smotherman said. “We say it every week, everybody out here’s so good, anybody can win on any given week. That’s what makes our sport so great. There’s Scottie Schefflers of the world that know how to win a lot more frequently every single year, but I think I’m getting a little bit of a taste of what they feel, a top player like that as far as just so much freedom every single week and feeling like what you’re doing, you’re getting the validation with the results, but also just the immense trust you have in the process that you’ve devised. item.content:encoded: Austin Smotherman won the playoff in Bermuda but Seamus Power got what he came for. Getty Images Austin Smotherman waited 100 PGA Tour events to get his first win . He needed just 57 holes to grab his second, beating Seamus Power on the third hole of a sudden-death playoff on Monday at the weather-shortened Butterfield Bermuda Championship. The win adds another year onto Smotherman’s full-time PGA Tour exempt status. His win at the Bank of Utah Championship gave him job security and a spot in the PGA Tour’s Championship Series when it begins in 2028. This win extends that through 2029. The victory in windy Bermuda also moved him up to No. 51 in the FedEx Cup Fall standings , putting him in position to earn starts at the first two Signature Events of 2027. Even Bermuda’s 40-mph gusts couldn’t extinguish the fall’s hottest player. “We knew we were doing a lot of good stuff and just wanted to go play golf,” Smotherman said of his attitude entering the FedEx Cup Fall after failing to make the FedEx Cup Playoffs. “We were excited for the fall season. We had our best FedEx Cup finish ever and the fall we felt was just going to be bonus golf and do things like this, and to have it come true and live this out now not once but twice in that short time frame is, I mean, I couldn’t have drawn it up. It’s a fairy tale, really.” Smotherman’s triumph in Utah was a victory 10 years in the making. He worked his way up from PGA Tour America (then called PGA Tour Latinoamerica) to the Korn Ferry Tour and then finally earned full-time PGA Tour status for the 2021-2022 PGA Tour season. Smotherman played three consecutive seasons on the PGA Tour before losing his card after finishing 169th in the FedEx Cup standings in 2024. But he bounced back, winning twice on the Korn Ferry Tour in 2025 to earn his card again. Smotherman played solid golf in his return to the PGA Tour in 2026, and he almost won the Cognizant Classic in March before finally kicking down the door in start No. 100 in Utah. Two weeks later, another win arrived, and with it proof of what Smotherman had long believed — something that can be invaluable as he looks to keep climbing the PGA Tour ladder. “It can literally happen at any time,” Smotherman said. “We say it every week, everybody out here’s so good, anybody can win on any given week. That’s what makes our sport so great. There’s Scottie Schefflers of the world that know how to win a lot more frequently every single year, but I think I’m getting a little bit of a taste of what they feel, a top player like that as far as just so much freedom every single week and feeling like what you’re doing, you’re getting the validation with the results, but also just the immense trust you have in the process that you’ve devised. I’ve been a professional now for 10 years, and I feel like I’ve put a lot of notches in my belt with different skills and things that help pay off at the end of the week.” But as Smotherman explained the feeling of another win and everything that comes with it, Seamus Power wasn’t far away. But he didn’t look like a man who came up short. Yes, a sloppy bogey on the third playoff hole kept him from claiming his second Bermuda title. But Power didn’t leave Port Royal Golf Course a loser. Perhaps there were none in Bermuda on Monday. Power won the 2022 Butterfield Bermuda Championship and finished 41st in the FedEx Cup in 2023. He backed that up with another top-60 season in 2024. But as his two-year exemption ran out, his game slipped. In 2025, Power had just two top-10s and six top-25s. He posted a T8 at the Valspar and then a T7 at the fall-ending RSM Classic, but in between that were missed cuts and finishes outside the top 30. He finished 117th in the FedEx Fall and lost his full-time exemption. Power still played a normal schedule in 2026 out of the 111-125 category. He said the only tournament he didn’t get into outside of the Signature Events was the WM Phoenix Open. Still, it was a season of uncertainty. One of hoping to play where you want but not knowing if that was possible. With a second-place finish in Bermuda, Power vaulted to 68th in the FedEx Fall standings, all but securing a full-time card in 2027. Asked earlier in the week about his goals on a blustery track where he’d previously found success, Power wasn’t eyeing a trophy. The goal was just to ensure 2027 was a smoother ride than 2026. A win would take care of that, but it wasn’t the only elixir for what he was forced to navigate in 2026. “I played a full schedule, but it was the unknowns and not knowing where I was going to get in and when I was going to get in was the tough part,” Power said after his second round on Friday. “So for me, trying to get back into that top 100, get yourself back to full status, and then I just feel like you’re in a better, more comfortable spot starting off in January. So like that’s going to be the big goal. Obviously, always trying to get a win, but this time of year, I mean, the win kind of takes care of both. So that top 100 is really going to be a big thing.” More than 48 hours later, after the final round was scrapped because of unfavorable weather, Power shook Smotherman’s hand after falling just shy of his third career PGA Tour win. While the leaderboard showed Smotherman’s name above the rest of the field, the other leaderboard everyone is eyeing this time of year showed Power had made the biggest jump of the week, rising 35 spots to check the most important box of the fall . He left a runner-up but with the freedom to exhale, relax and refocus on the next task at hand, knowing his 2027 picture will be much clearer. “It gets me back to full status again, which was frustrating this year playing — not really knowing when you’re in, when you’re not in,” Power said Sunday. “That’s nice. That was a big goal for the fall to get a top 100 locked up. Now I’ll have a look at the list and see if I can maybe move into that top 60 or 70, whatever that cutoff is for the first couple [Signature Events]. But really big strides for me forward in the fall — three events, two top 10s, almost winning here, so a lot of good stuff.” The post In Bermuda, a sudden-death playoff ended with no loser appeared first on Golf .

item.title: Notre Dame’s Marcus Freeman calls out coaching staff with important challenge
item.description: Michael Caterina-Imagn Images Notre Dame’s Marcus Freeman calls out coaching staff with important challenge appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Notre Dame is coming off a bye week after their first loss of the season. They fell to BYU 28-24 in a game filled with back-and-forths and a controversial ending. Head coach Marcus Freeman is still talking about the ending to the BYU and Notre Dame game . In the game, CJ Carr passed for 261 yards but did not have a passing touchdown. Meanwhile, just five wide receivers and tight ends had receptions, leading to a challenge from Freeman to the rest of the coaching staff, per Pete Sampson of The Athletic. “‘I have a lot of confidence in the entire wide receiver room.’ – Marcus Freeman. Said he challenged the staff to rotate more moving forward,” Sampson posted on X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Jaden Greathouse and Jordan Faison were solid in the game. Greathouse brought in eight receptions for 125 yards while Faison had six receptions for 64 yards. Third receiver Micah Gilbert brought in three receptions for 31 yards. The rest of the receptions went to tight ends and running backs, plus CJ Carr getting one reception in the game. It was a short rotation at the receiver position , something Freeman also addressed. “Marcus Freeman asked about the short rotation at wide receiver: Said the plan was to get Mylan Graham into the game before halftime, but the drive was two-minute. Said second half deficit meant the staff wanted to keep the guys the staff ‘truly trust’ to play,” Sampson added. Meanwhile, none of the receivers brought in touchdown receptions, as the offense failed to get a touchdown in the red zone three times . “Marcus Freeman said Notre Dame focused on a lot of red zone and two-minute situations during the bye week. Irish failed on both repeatedly against BYU, including end of half and end of game,” Sampson concluded. The loss dropped the Irish to 6-1 on the season, but Notre Dame is still one of the top teams in the nation, and if they keep winning, they will be heading to the College Football Playoff. Next up for the Irish is a home game against Navy before they host number one Miami the following week. Related: Paul Finebaum goes to bat for Texas’ CFP chances regardless of record Related: Robert Griffin III’s Heisman Trophy picks will have Miami, Oregon State fans going crazy

item.title: Putellas wins record-equalling third Ballon d'Or
item.description: Alexia Putellas won four trophies with Barcelona last season and 38 over the course of 14 years [Getty Images] Spain midfielder Alexia Putellas has won the Ballon d'Or Feminin for a record-equalling third time, keeping the prize in Spanish hands for a sixth consecutive year. Putellas, 32, captained Barcelona to Champions League glory as part of a quadruple in 2025-26, before joining Women's Super League (WSL) side London City Lionesses in July . She joins Spain team-mate Aitana Bonmati on three Ballon d'Or Feminin crowns - her former Barcelona colleague won the award in 2023, 2024 and 2025 after Putellas did so in 2021 and 2022. The past six Ballons d'Or have been won by the Spanish pair, with Norway's Ada Hegerberg (2018) and Megan Rapinoe of the United States (2019) the only non-Spaniards to claim the prize. Putellas' latest victory caps a remarkable return to the pinnacle of world football after suffering a career-threatening anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury in 2022. "All the boys and girls around the world - if you love football and if you want to play football, play football. It doesn't matter if you're a boy or if you're a girl," Putellas said. "Doesn't matter where you come from. Don't listen if someone tells you, you can't do it. Believe in yourself." She collected the most votes from an international panel of journalists across Fifa's top-50 ranked countries, with Barcelona striker Ewa Pajor coming second and Manchester City forward Khadija Shaw third. Meanwhile, England captain Harry Kane won the men's Ballon d'Or , becoming the first English player to do so since Michael Owen in 2001. The numbers don't lie While Barcelona are always overwhelming favourites to win the three competitions on offer in Spain, Putellas' performances last season showed that she is still among the world's elite. Nicknamed 'La Reina' - meaning the queen - Putellas scored 21 goals and provided 13 assists in all competitions, ranking her third and second respectively among players across Europe's top five leagues. Seven of those goals came in the Women's Champions League as Barcelona claimed a fourth continental title in six seasons. Only Pernille Harder (eight), Alessia Russo (nine) and Ewa Pajor (11) scored more, all of whom are strikers by trade. But Putellas' contributions to Barcelona's attacking play went far beyond scoring goals herself. In Liga F - which Barcelona won for a seventh consecutive season - she finished joint-sixth for assists (seven) and fourth for open-play chances created (40). Across Europe's top five leagues, only Claudia Pina (199), Vicky Lopez (183) and Georgia Stanway (168) recorded more sequence involvements ending in an open-play shot than Putellas (151). In all competitions, she created more chances (89, 19 of which were big chances) and completed more passes ending in the final third (965) than any other player in Liga F, the Champions League, Copa de la Reina and Supercopa de Espana. item.content:encoded: Alexia Putellas won four trophies with Barcelona last season and 38 over the course of 14 years [Getty Images] Spain midfielder Alexia Putellas has won the Ballon d'Or Feminin for a record-equalling third time, keeping the prize in Spanish hands for a sixth consecutive year. Putellas, 32, captained Barcelona to Champions League glory as part of a quadruple in 2025-26, before joining Women's Super League (WSL) side London City Lionesses in July . She joins Spain team-mate Aitana Bonmati on three Ballon d'Or Feminin crowns - her former Barcelona colleague won the award in 2023, 2024 and 2025 after Putellas did so in 2021 and 2022. The past six Ballons d'Or have been won by the Spanish pair, with Norway's Ada Hegerberg (2018) and Megan Rapinoe of the United States (2019) the only non-Spaniards to claim the prize. Putellas' latest victory caps a remarkable return to the pinnacle of world football after suffering a career-threatening anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury in 2022. "All the boys and girls around the world - if you love football and if you want to play football, play football. It doesn't matter if you're a boy or if you're a girl," Putellas said. "Doesn't matter where you come from. Don't listen if someone tells you, you can't do it. Believe in yourself." She collected the most votes from an international panel of journalists across Fifa's top-50 ranked countries, with Barcelona striker Ewa Pajor coming second and Manchester City forward Khadija Shaw third. Meanwhile, England captain Harry Kane won the men's Ballon d'Or , becoming the first English player to do so since Michael Owen in 2001. The numbers don't lie While Barcelona are always overwhelming favourites to win the three competitions on offer in Spain, Putellas' performances last season showed that she is still among the world's elite. Nicknamed 'La Reina' - meaning the queen - Putellas scored 21 goals and provided 13 assists in all competitions, ranking her third and second respectively among players across Europe's top five leagues. Seven of those goals came in the Women's Champions League as Barcelona claimed a fourth continental title in six seasons. Only Pernille Harder (eight), Alessia Russo (nine) and Ewa Pajor (11) scored more, all of whom are strikers by trade. But Putellas' contributions to Barcelona's attacking play went far beyond scoring goals herself. In Liga F - which Barcelona won for a seventh consecutive season - she finished joint-sixth for assists (seven) and fourth for open-play chances created (40). Across Europe's top five leagues, only Claudia Pina (199), Vicky Lopez (183) and Georgia Stanway (168) recorded more sequence involvements ending in an open-play shot than Putellas (151). In all competitions, she created more chances (89, 19 of which were big chances) and completed more passes ending in the final third (965) than any other player in Liga F, the Champions League, Copa de la Reina and Supercopa de Espana. Only Bayern Munich's Klara Buhl created as many chances as Putellas in the Champions League last season (36), the most by a player in a single edition of the competition since Caroline Graham Hansen in 2021-22 (38). From watching Iniesta to winning it all Putellas was born and grew up in the Catalan municipality of Mollet del Valles, about 12 miles north-east of Barcelona. She began playing football in the street, and soon became a Barcelona fan and a regular attendee at Camp Nou. With matches always on the TV at home, former Spain and Barcelona star Andres Iniesta and Brazilian duo Rivaldo and Ronaldinho quickly became her idols. After attending a summer football camp run by Xavi and playing for local side CE Sabadell, Putellas spent a year at La Masia, Barcelona's famous youth academy. Spells at Espanyol and Levante followed the disbandment of her girls team, before she eventually returned to Barca in 2012. Cue the start of a 14-year career with her childhood club during which she won 38 trophies, including 10 league titles and four European cups. But after winning the Ballon d'Or for the first time in 2021, one of the toughest moments of Putellas' career came when she suffered an ACL injury on the eve of Euro 2022, ruling her out of the tournament. Though she retained the Ballon d'Or later that year, it took a while for her to return to her best level. Playing only a bit-part role in Spain's triumphant 2023 World Cup campaign would have stung. After scoring in the 2024 Champions League final and improving further the following season, in 2025-26 she shouldered much of Barcelona's creative burden as Aitana Bonmati missed five months through injury and ended the season a quadruple winner. If that was not enough, the midfielder scored twice in a 4-0 thrashing of England in June that secured Spain's place at the 2027 World Cup at the Lionesses' expense. With her contract at Barcelona expiring and keen for a fresh challenge, Putellas made the decision to leave her childhood club. She, and her fans, were distraught. She had several offers from England, Mexico and the United States, but joined the ambitious project of US billionaire Michelle Kang at London City Lionesses in July. "I'm just always looking forward to better things and that's why I'm here too, because I always need to be moving as a person and a player," Putellas told BBC's Women's Football Weekly podcast in August. With three goals and one assist in seven WSL games for her new club, it is clear Putellas is still deserving of her nickname. Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

item.title: Jason Kelce attends Eagles fans’ wedding at MNF tailgate
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles superfans got married while tailgating before the NFL Monday Night Football game against the Dallas Cowboys. Not much is known about the bride and groom except that their married name coincidentally is Byrd. Enthusiastic fans cheered for them, and a band played the Eagles fight song after the ceremony. MORE: How to live stream MNF for free: Watch Eagles vs Cowboys, TV channel A festive atmosphere and beautiful weather were part of the big event outside Lincoln Financial Field. Eagles legend Jason Kelce was spotted handing out cans of the Kelce brothers’ Garage Beer. The couple was selected as part of a Garage Beer sweepstakes . Go Byrds! 💚💍 (Seriously, their last name is Byrd) https://t.co/Ye5Ek1YyAq — NBC Sports Philadelphia (@NBCSPhilly) October 26, 2026 Eagles vs. Cowboys has a different tone Oct 11, 2026; Tottenham, ENG; Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) drops back to pass during the second half against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) With Jalen Hurts out indefinitely with blood clots in his lungs, and lingering confusion over what actually happened behind the scenes , this traditional NFC East battle feels different. Fans still do not know what to think about Hurts’ long-term prognosis or future in football or with the Eagles. Many wonder if he will be on the sidelines or in a box during the game. MORE: Bold predictions for Monday Night Football in NFL Week 7 NFC East having a ho-hum year The Eagles have plenty of reasons to be playing subpar football. Their injury report is as long as the Declaration of Independence. However, the Cowboys do not have any excuses for their less-than-impressive play. The defense is porous, and a rusty Saquon Barkley may just run right through them. The Cowboys have not won a game at Lincoln Financial Field in almost five years. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories on The Big Lead —

MORE: Bold predictions for Monday Night Football in NFL Week 7 NFC East having a ho-hum year The Eagles have plenty of reasons to be playing subpar football. Their injury report is as long as the Declaration of Independence. However, the Cowboys do not have any excuses for their less-than-impressive play. The defense is porous, and a rusty Saquon Barkley may just run right through them. The Cowboys have not won a game at Lincoln Financial Field in almost five years. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories on The Big Lead —

item.title: Week 9 SEC power rankings: Georgia reclaims No. 1, Texas back in top five
item.description: Despite being idle on Saturday, the Georgia Bulldogs have reclaimed the No. 1 spot in our SEC football power rankings following a chaotic Week 8 slate. When in doubt, pick Kirby Smart's squad as the conference's top team. Georgia's lone loss this season came against unranked Auburn in Week 7, but the Bulldogs' road win over Alabama provides an advantage over Will Stein and the Kentucky Wildcats , who we have as the second-best team in the league in this week's power rankings. Arguably the scariest SEC squad to play right now resides in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. After its loss to Kentucky, LSU's offense has clicked and put on electric performances, outscoring Mississippi State and Auburn by a combined 69-17 margin, which is why we have the Tigers as the No. 3 team in the SEC. Texas ranks fourth, ahead of Ole Miss, after securing a thrilling 34-27 win over the Rebels in Austin over the weekend. The Alabama Crimson Tide are just outside the top five, followed by the South Carolina Gamecocks, who knocked off Tennessee on a game-winning field goal at Williams-Brice Stadium over the weekend. The Vols ' loss to Shane Beamer and company bumped them down to No. 8, ahead of the Missouri Tigers at No. 9. Behind Mizzou, the Florida Gators round out the top 10, with a massive test against Georgia approaching for Jon Sumrall and company on Saturday. item.title: Pistons' Cade Cunningham calls out doubters before Knicks game
item.description: Pistons' Cade Cunningham calls out doubters before Knicks game originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Detroit Pistons are off to a hot 3-0 start for the NBA season, and that's something that should put a big smile on their faces. But going into the season, not everybody thought this team would, well, be this good. There's a reason there's the saying "Detroit vs. Everybody." Sometimes being a Detroit sports fan feels like the world is against you. Cade Cunningham gets it. The Pistons' starting guard spoke with the media after the team's 106-93 win over the Philadelphia 76ers . Cade Cunningham sends a message to Detroit Pistons naysayers Following the 76ers game and days before Detroit takes on New York, Cunningham called out Pistons doubters. "It don't matter," he said, according to Hunter Patterson of The Athletic on X . "We're going to keep on going and let whatever people that are talking about us say whatever they want to say about us." Sometimes there's no real way to silence the naysayers. Even winning games won't always do it. But winning games is something you can't fake, and numbers don't lie, so if the Pistons keep winning, it'll be pie in the face for those who said Detroit would never be good enough. Next up, the Pistons take on the reigning NBA champions, the New York Knicks , on Tuesday night at Madison Square Garden. What's wild is that the Knicks haven't won a single game yet this season. So, New York will come into this matchup with a chip on their shoulder and desperate for a win, but that doesn't mean they'll get it. More NBA news: LeBron James and Joel Embiid already have a viral moment with the 76ers Detroit's J.B. Bickerstaff sends bold message on 'Pistons basketball' after win over Celtics 76ers' LeBron James accuses NBA refs of giving Knicks a championship whistle in season opener

item.title: Virginia basketball player profile: Thijs De Ridder is ready to carry the load
item.description: CHARLOTTESVILLE, VIRGINIA - FEBRUARY 24: Thijs de Ridder #28 of the Virginia Cavaliers dunks in the second half during the game against the NC State Wolfpack at John Paul Jones Arena on February 24, 2026 in Charlottesville, Virginia. (Photo by Ryan M. Kelly/Getty Images) | Getty Images A year ago, Thijs De Ridder was not sure he belonged. He had spent five seasons as a professional in Belgium and Spain, and he was the last piece of Ryan Odom’s first roster in the summer of 2025, spending much of it waiting on NCAA clearance. He had not been in a classroom in four years. Home was no longer a one-hour flight away. And he had no idea how his game would translate. “I was just scared, really nervous in the beginning a little bit,” De Ridder told the Associated Press at ACC Tipoff this month. “I didn’t even know that my style of basketball would fit in the college basketball part.” It fit. De Ridder started all 36 games, led Virginia in scoring and rebounding and became the first Cavalier to make the All-ACC first team since Sam Hauser in 2021. This month, the league’s media voted him ACC Preseason Player of the Year with 30 of 48 votes, and he was the only unanimous pick for the preseason All-ACC first team. The last Cavalier to win the preseason award was Malcolm Brogdon, who shared it with North Carolina’s Marcus Paige in 2015-16. De Ridder is the first Cavalier to win it outright. View this post on Instagram Now the workload will get even heavier. Virginia is ranked No. 9 in the AP preseason poll and was picked second in the ACC, but Ugonna Onyenso and Devin Tillis are gone from the frontcourt, and Odom does not have much behind his top two bigs. De Ridder was already one of Virginia’s go-to options last year. This season, he will likely be asked to do it for more minutes than ever, in his final college season, with an NBA future riding on it. This is the ninth installment of Streaking the Lawn’s preseason profile series. Our profiles of Chance Mallory , Christian Harmon , Jurian Dixon , Kalu Anya , Sam Lewis , Elijah Gertrude , Martin Carrere and Johann Grünloh can be found here. item.content:encoded: CHARLOTTESVILLE, VIRGINIA - FEBRUARY 24: Thijs de Ridder #28 of the Virginia Cavaliers dunks in the second half during the game against the NC State Wolfpack at John Paul Jones Arena on February 24, 2026 in Charlottesville, Virginia. (Photo by Ryan M. Kelly/Getty Images) | Getty Images A year ago, Thijs De Ridder was not sure he belonged. He had spent five seasons as a professional in Belgium and Spain, and he was the last piece of Ryan Odom’s first roster in the summer of 2025, spending much of it waiting on NCAA clearance. He had not been in a classroom in four years. Home was no longer a one-hour flight away. And he had no idea how his game would translate. “I was just scared, really nervous in the beginning a little bit,” De Ridder told the Associated Press at ACC Tipoff this month. “I didn’t even know that my style of basketball would fit in the college basketball part.” It fit. De Ridder started all 36 games, led Virginia in scoring and rebounding and became the first Cavalier to make the All-ACC first team since Sam Hauser in 2021. This month, the league’s media voted him ACC Preseason Player of the Year with 30 of 48 votes, and he was the only unanimous pick for the preseason All-ACC first team. The last Cavalier to win the preseason award was Malcolm Brogdon, who shared it with North Carolina’s Marcus Paige in 2015-16. De Ridder is the first Cavalier to win it outright. View this post on Instagram Now the workload will get even heavier. Virginia is ranked No. 9 in the AP preseason poll and was picked second in the ACC, but Ugonna Onyenso and Devin Tillis are gone from the frontcourt, and Odom does not have much behind his top two bigs. De Ridder was already one of Virginia’s go-to options last year. This season, he will likely be asked to do it for more minutes than ever, in his final college season, with an NBA future riding on it. This is the ninth installment of Streaking the Lawn’s preseason profile series. Our profiles of Chance Mallory , Christian Harmon , Jurian Dixon , Kalu Anya , Sam Lewis , Elijah Gertrude , Martin Carrere and Johann Grünloh can be found here. Year one: Virginia’s go-to scorer De Ridder did not take long to answer his own question. In his college debut against Rider, he had 21 points and 10 rebounds, team highs in both. By the end of the season, he had averaged 15.6 points and 6.2 rebounds while shooting 50.8 percent from the field and 35.7 percent from three. He scored 20 or more points 12 times, the most by a Cavalier since Brogdon’s 18 in 2015-16. He also made the ACC All-Rookie team, a reminder of how unusual his path was and of the state of modern college basketball. He was a 23-year-old “freshman” with five years of pro basketball behind him. What made him so hard to guard was that he could score from anywhere. De Ridder is a perfect example of the modern, analytics-driven game that Odom covets. He is a bruiser down low: nearly half of his attempts came at the rim, where he made 61 percent, including 14 dunks. He can also stretch the floor, making 40 of his 112 threes. And because he was so physical going to the basket, he lived at the free-throw line, attempting 172 free throws, converting them at a 70.9 percent clip. His best stretch came in late January. On Jan. 27 at Notre Dame, he scored a career-high 32 points in a 100-97 double-overtime win, making 14 of his 15 free throws. Four days later, he added 17 at Boston College, and the ACC named him its Player of the Week and Rookie of the Week. View this post on Instagram Then defenses adjusted. Through Jan. 31, De Ridder averaged 17.0 points on 53.8 percent shooting. Over his final 15 games, he averaged 13.5 points on 46.1 percent. His free-throw attempts dropped from 5.4 a game to 3.9, and his shooting at the rim fell from 67 percent to 53 percent. Within two weeks of his Player of the Week award, he scored in single digits in three straight games against Syracuse, Florida State and Ohio State. As the season went on, I saw opponents send a second defender at him in the post far more often, and he did not always have an answer. Instead of finding the open shooter, he too often forced the issue, and his ball handling, especially on his spin moves, let him down. The numbers against the best teams tell the same story. In four games against AP-ranked opponents, he averaged 12.5 points on 42.1 percent shooting, with 12 turnovers and four assists. In the ACC championship game against Duke, he went 1-of-6 for five points, with three turnovers and no assists, in a 74-70 loss. To his credit, he answered a week later. Against Tennessee in the NCAA Tournament’s second round, he scored 22 points and made a career-high four threes, including the one that put Virginia ahead 71-70 with 2:03 left. Virginia lost 79-72, but it was a reminder of what he looks like when everything is working. Year two: more depth, less in the frontcourt On paper, Virginia is deeper than it was a year ago. The Cavaliers retained every eligible player and added eight newcomers, and Odom has used 11 to 13 players in meaningful minutes across the preseason. But more playable depth is not the same as last year’s high-level depth. Last season, Virginia could bring Mallory, Jacari White, Devin Tillis and Onyenso off the bench, and on some nights they were as important as anyone in the starting lineup. I do not expect this bench to match that. The gap is clearest up front. The backcourt and wing rotation runs eight deep, with Mallory, Lewis and Adekunle holding down the starting lineup and Vide, Dixon, Gertrude, Harmon and Carrere all pushing for minutes. Behind De Ridder and Grünloh, the frontcourt options are Kalu Anya, Silas Barksdale and freshman Favour Ibe. Anya redshirted last year at Saint Louis and looked overmatched at times in the paint against Vanderbilt, Barksdale redshirted as a freshman, and Ibe is a true freshman. None of them has played a minute of Division I basketball for Virginia. Last season, Onyenso’s presence meant Odom never had to lean too hard on either of his starting bigs. De Ridder played 27.7 minutes a game, and he topped 30 minutes only 10 times in 36 games, two of them in overtime games. That luxury is gone. Torvik’s model projects him to play 82 percent of Virginia’s minutes, or about 33 a game, and to average 18.5 points and 7.8 rebounds. It also projects his usage to drop slightly, from 26.5 percent to 25. In other words, the model expects him to play more minutes, not a heavier load on each possession. At last season’s per-minute scoring rate, 33 minutes works out to almost exactly 18.5 points. The preseason was encouraging. Across three exhibitions, De Ridder scored 37 points on 14-of-23 shooting and 5-of-8 from three, capped by 17 points on 7-of-8 shooting in 19 minutes at Villanova. Exhibitions are exhibitions, and Odom kept his minutes under 20 in both blowouts. The regular season will not be so forgiving. His versatility may also be stretched. De Ridder told the Belgian outlet DH in March that he was mainly considered a power forward in Europe and was developing to play small forward as well. Odom used him at the three in a jumbo lineup against Vanderbilt, and with Onyenso gone, he is also an option at center in smaller lineups. That flexibility is valuable, but on a thin frontcourt, it also means more of the dirty work falls to him. What I will be watching De Ridder already has an All-ACC résumé. Here is what will decide whether he takes the next step. Working out of the double team. This is the biggest one. When teams began loading up on him, his problems came in two forms. In January, he tried to force his way through it: in the eight games from Dec. 31 to Jan. 27, he committed 27 turnovers. From February on, teams took him away instead. His turnovers came down, but so did his scoring, and his assists did not go up. He averaged 1.6 assists a game both before and after Feb. 1, and he finished the season with more turnovers (64) than a

item.title: Tuchel 'out of superlatives' as England's Kane wins Ballon d'Or
item.description: FILE PHOTO - England's Harry Kane celebrates scoring his side's second goal during the UEFA Nations League group A3 soccer match between Czech Republic and England at the Fortuna Arena. (is associated with: «Tuchel 'out of superlatives' as England's Kane wins Ballon d'Or») Bradley Collyer/PA Wire/dpa England head coach Thomas Tuchel led the tributes to Harry Kane after he became the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d'Or. The Bayern Munich striker saw off competition from Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe and Barcelona's Lamine Yamal to become only the fifth Englishman to be honoured with the award. "Congratulations Harry on a deserved Ballon d'Or!" said Tuchel. "I ran out of superlatives to describe your performances a long time ago, but I'm delighted to see that you have now been formally recognised by the football world. "To become the first Englishman to win this huge honour in 25 years makes it extra special and we are lucky to have you as our leader. "I know you will enjoy this moment with your loved ones and then get back to doing what you do best - scoring goals and winning football matches." Prince William, patron of the Football Association, also sent his congratulations. "What a fantastic achievement and so deserved," the prince of Wales wrote on Instagram. "A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments." Jamie Carragher, who was a team-mate of Michael Owen when he won the Ballon d'Or in 2001, felt it was long overdue. "Absolutely delighted. What a career he's had, what a player he is, and as a country, we haven't got enough Ballon d'Or winners," he told Sky Sports. "My former team-mate Michael Owen was the last to win it in 2001, so it's been a long wait. "But in terms of Harry Kane, and I think Jude Bellingham, who's going to be a future Ballon d'Or winner, we do have two of the greatest players of their era. I'm delighted for Kane and the country." Carragher felt Kane's move to the Bundesliga three years ago helped tip the scales in his favour. "It's a move he needed to make. I thought he might be obsessed with the Premier League goalscoring record, but he's obsessed with goalscoring records, not just that one," he added. "But it also gives him a great chance of winning the Champions League and being involved in Ballon d'Or selections. "There's no way Harry Kane could've won the Ballon d'Or if he was playing for Tottenham." Former France forward and Ballon d'Or ceremony co-host Thierry Henry said: "I would always back my fellow Frenchmen but I have to say something about Harry Kane. "I have seen him since the beginning. He had to suffer really hard to achieve what he has achieved. A worthy winner, well done."

NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Cole Burston/Getty Images) Getty The New York Knicks are still searching for their first victory of the season. Their efforts to break out of an early slump won’t get any easier with another setback to their backcourt depth. Jose Alvarado has been ruled out for Tuesday’s game against the Detroit Pistons at Madison Square Garden, according to the NBA’s official injury report. The veteran guard continues to deal with a left ankle sprain and will miss his second consecutive game. For a Knicks team already 0-3, his absence leaves coach Mike Brown searching for answers. Jose Alvarado Injury Update Brings Another Knicks Absence Getty Jose Alvarado of the New York Knicks steals the ball from Tyrese Maxey of the Philadelphia 76ers during the fourth quarter of the game at Madison Square Garden on October 20, 2026 in New York City. Alvarado missed Sunday’s 111-102 loss to the Orlando Magic after initially being listed as questionable. Monday’s injury report confirmed he would remain sidelined against Detroit. The Knicks have not announced a timetable for his return. Alvarado played in New York’s first two games, averaging 5.0 points, 2.5 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.5 steals in 13.6 minutes. He contributed eight points, three assists and two steals in the season-opening loss to Philadelphia. However, Alvarado struggled against Boston, finishing with two points and three turnovers in 11 minutes. His value goes beyond scoring. Alvarado brings defensive pressure, energy and an aggressive approach that can disrupt opposing guards. Without him, New York has turned to several other backcourt options. The results have been mixed. Tyler Kolek Shines as Playma

NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Cole Burston/Getty Images) Getty The New York Knicks are still searching for their first victory of the season. Their efforts to break out of an early slump won’t get any easier with another setback to their backcourt depth. Jose Alvarado has been ruled out for Tuesday’s game against the Detroit Pistons at Madison Square Garden, according to the NBA’s official injury report. The veteran guard continues to deal with a left ankle sprain and will miss his second consecutive game. For a Knicks team already 0-3, his absence leaves coach Mike Brown searching for answers. Jose Alvarado Injury Update Brings Another Knicks Absence Getty Jose Alvarado of the New York Knicks steals the ball from Tyrese Maxey of the Philadelphia 76ers during the fourth quarter of the game at Madison Square Garden on October 20, 2026 in New York City. Alvarado missed Sunday’s 111-102 loss to the Orlando Magic after initially being listed as questionable. Monday’s injury report confirmed he would remain sidelined against Detroit. The Knicks have not announced a timetable for his return. Alvarado played in New York’s first two games, averaging 5.0 points, 2.5 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.5 steals in 13.6 minutes. He contributed eight points, three assists and two steals in the season-opening loss to Philadelphia. However, Alvarado struggled against Boston, finishing with two points and three turnovers in 11 minutes. His value goes beyond scoring. Alvarado brings defensive pressure, energy and an aggressive approach that can disrupt opposing guards. Without him, New York has turned to several other backcourt options. The results have been mixed. Tyler Kolek Shines as Playmaker, Jordan Clarkson Struggles Getty Tyler Kolek of the New York Knicks looks to make a pass around Jakob Poeltl of the Toronto Raptors during the first half of their Pre-season NBA game at Scotiabank Arena on October 13, 2026 in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. Kolek made the strongest case for additional minutes during Sunday’s loss to Orlando. The second-year guard recorded nine assists, three rebounds and one steal in 15 minutes. However, he went scoreless, missing all four field-goal attempts, including two from beyond the arc. Still, his nine assists led the Knicks, providing a glimpse of his potential as a facilitator. Clarkson had a much quieter evening. The veteran guard played just five minutes, 19 seconds, finishing with zero points and one rebound. He missed his only field-goal attempt, a 3-pointer. McBride also struggled offensively. He managed one point, one rebound, one assist and one steal in nearly 13 minutes. McBride missed his lone field-goal attempt and converted one of two free throws. Combined, the three guards scored just one point on 0-for-6 shooting. Their uneven production leaves Brown with an important decision about his bench rotation. Kolek offered encouraging playmaking, but the Knicks still need more scoring from their reserves. Knicks Face Unbeaten Pistons With Backcourt Questions New York’s next opponent presents another difficult challenge. Detroit enters Tuesday’s game 3-0 following victories over Boston, Miami and Philadelphia. However, the Pistons have their own injury concerns. Starting center Jalen Duren has been ruled out with a right hamstring strain, while Ausar Thompson is questionable because of a right ankle sprain. For the Knicks, Alvarado’s absence creates an opportunity for Kolek, Clarkson and McBride to establish themselves. Kolek’s nine assists offered a promising development in an otherwise disappointing loss. Yet New York cannot afford another ineffective performance from its bench. The Knicks are trying to avoid their first 0-4 start in years, and Brown needs a more reliable rotation. Until Alvarado returns, the pressure falls on the guards behind Jalen Brunson to help turn New York’s season around. item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: Russo to Arsenal’s rescue and Olid makes Manchester United progress
item.description: Gunners edged north London derby while new United manager put the brakes on Manchester City’s winning start The penalty that allowed Arsenal to come from a goal behind to take the lead may have come with a healthy helping of luck, with the ball having come off Ella Morris’s raised arm as her teammate attempted to clear it, but it could prove to be the turning point Arsenal needed. “It’s been tough. We haven’t got the results we wanted,” penalty scorer Alessia Russo told the BBC afterwards. “This was an important win as far as north London derbies goes. It was really important and this was a great opportunity to try and turn it around.” It has taken seven games for the Gunners to secure their second league win of the season despite high hopes ahead of the new campaign and, while the result was a significant one, there is still a long way to go if Arsenal are to salvage anything from the most disappointing of starts. The performance against Tottenham was far from perfect and, in the first half in particular, sloppy and lacking fight. Tightening up their passing and harnessing the grit they found as they clung onto their lead towards the end of the match will be critical if they are to really kick on from this result. Suzanne Wrack Continue reading...

item.title: McTominay stars in Napoli draw that leaves Allegri ‘not lucid enough’ to talk | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Gli Azzurri show positive signs of improvement in seesaw 3-3 draw against a Roma side inspired by Messi-like Matías Soulé Scott McTominay was leaving nothing to doubt. He appeared to have scored with a close-range header early in the second half of Napoli’s game at home to Roma, but Pierluigi Gollini clawed the ball out from inside the goal. McTominay got his noggin to the rebound, nudging it back across the line. Roma’s keeper pushed away again, so the Napoli midfielder got to his feet and smashed the loose ball into the back of the net. Just typical. You wait two months for your first goal of the Serie A season, then three show up at once. They only counted for one, of course, but McTominay looked happy enough with that as he ran to thank Matteo Politano for the assist. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Bournemouth’s transfer nous puts United to shame, Araújo is winning admirers at Anfield and Suzuki adapts swiftly at Villa The three Bournemouth goalscorers cost a combined £85m, joining from Vasco da Gama, Middlesbrough, and Porto. The Cherries are smart at investing, far more so than Manchester United, who have wasted a lot of money by failing to look outside the box for players like Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson. United may not have the wealth they previously showed in the transfer market but Bournemouth are showing what can be done within a budget and, more importantly, will be able to make a profit on signings. United, however, only know losses as everyone’s price tag diminishes the moment they come through the Old Trafford door. Jason Wilcox and others can point to certain factors that are against them but there are quality signings to be made at the right price if you have the ability to find them. item.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...

item.title: Pierre Sage regrets ‘missed 15 minutes’ as defeat increases heat on Crystal Palace manager
item.description: Sage’s side beaten 2-0 at home by Newcastle ‘Every mistake that is bad will be a goal’ Pierre Sage blamed a 15-minute loss of concentration for Crystal Palace’s 2-0 defeat by Newcastle and insisted he remains the right man to lead the south London club. “We missed 15 minutes when we came back from the dressing room,” the Frenchman said. “When you let your opponent take the initiative without pressure, without reply, it’s difficult.” Palace have conceded 19 goals in eight games and have the worst defensive record in the Premier League, an obvious contrast to last season when Sage’s Lens side had the second-best defensive record in Ligue 1. “When we concede all these goals … you can interpret that through the style of play and also how well we are playing, especially defensively,” Sage said. item.title: Fernandes gamble leaves Carrick to carry the can for United’s institutional failures | Will Unwin
item.description: Leaving out his captain was doomed to fail but so are the club under the current leadership and the fans at Old Trafford know that all too well Dropping your captain, who has held the team together for most of the past five years, is a bold move from a man whose job is on the line. It was very much a make-or-break decision from Michael Carrick to leave out Bruno Fernandes against Bournemouth. It did not work and Carrick knew the consequences if it failed and will probably pay the price for it, but he should not be alone. Carrick said the decision to drop the Portuguese playmaker was purely based on football reasons but criticising his manager after the desperate defeat to Como cannot have helped. Clearly Carrick disagreed with his captain’s comments on the lack of pressing in the Champions League fixture. It was somewhat telling that Lisandro Martínez kept his place despite pointing out the director of football, Jason Wilcox, was a hindrance to the club the previous week. Continue reading...

After another Europa League setback at home to Celta Vigo on Thursday, the champions bounced back with a victory that restored their four-point cushion over Rangers at the top. item.title: Osula and Barnes strike as Newcastle pile pressure on lacklustre Palace
item.description: The first half was dreadful. The pass completion rate was a meagre 72.8%, although it felt lower. There were only two shots on target. The sun kept popping out from behind the clouds to take a look, and then going back in again, appalled. And the really bad news for Crystal Palace is that, for them, that was the good bit. Newcastle were much improved after the break. Will Osula touched in a Jacob Murphy cross two minutes after half-time, Joe Willock had an effort ruled out for a marginal offside five minutes later, and Harvey Barnes completed a slick passing move six minutes after that. A smattering of boos from the home fans made clear what everybody already knew. Quarter of an hour of proper football had been enough to win the game, and that leaves Pierre Sage under significant pressure . Continue reading...

item.title: Isak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an end
item.description: Brighton’s impressive run was blown off course at Anfield where Liverpool performed with an appetite and urgency at both ends of the pitch that showed Andoni Iraola’s methods taking root. It was Liverpool, deserving winners on home soil for the first time in the Premier League this season, who looked upwardly mobile. There was more evidence of the expensive trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola feeling at home and adapting to Iraola’s demands. Wirtz was instrumental in an opening goal officially credited to Brighton’s Pascal Gross and Isak scored for the sixth time in six Premier League appearances to shatter the visitors’ sequence of four successive league wins. The sight of Barcola sprinting back to help his defence and Ronald Araújo smashing into challenges, as Liverpool stubbornly defended their lead and their box in the second half, satisfied Iraola just as much as his side’s incisiveness before the break. Continue reading...

item.title: Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s antics are no laughing matter for fans
item.description: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest. Continue reading...

Tottenham had a corner on the left-hand side, in a game that had felt to that point like an extended practice session, a refinement of systems, the football equivalent of watching two middle-aged men methodically emptying the dishwasher, adding salt, descaling the hoses, tutting over knives incorrectly slotted, cups in the wrong row. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...
